articleTitle: Detecting Multiple Overlapping Birds in Audio Recordings using Self Attention-based Wavelet Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: In this study, we explore the effectiveness of Wavelet Convolutional Neural Network (WCNN) and Self Attention-based Wavelet Convolutional Neural Network (SA-WCNN) for multi-label bird species classification. Our approach involves applying SA- WCNN to the mel spectrogram, yielding coefficients at different decomposition levels, including approximation and detail coefficients in various directions. By integrating multiresolution analysis with CNNs, our SA-WCNN stands as a powerful tool for capturing the nuanced features required for accurate and robust multilabel bird classification. The proposed work reports an average Fl-score of 0.68 for the SA-WCNN model, 0.61 for WCNN and it outperforms the baseline CNN model. Experimental evaluation is done using the bird's sound database, Xeno-canto.

articleTitle: Multithreaded State Feedback Control with Speed Estimation for Permanent Magnet DC Motor Speed Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: The lack of popularity of full state feedback control structure among power electronics engineers primarily stems from the inherent difficulty in imposing constraints on state variables. Multithreaded state controller (MTSC) approach addresses this challenge and has offered a straightforward and efficient method to impose constraints in a full state feedback control system. This article explores into the application of the MTSC approach for speed control in a permanent magnet brushed DC (PMDC) motor, using estimated value of speed. Two new speed estimation algorithms are introduced in this paper, which utilizes sampled values of armature current and armature voltage at certain defined time intervals during a switching interval of the power converter, to arrive at the estimated value of speed. The simulation study done in MATLAB, validated the correctness of the proposed speed estimation algorithms and also the effectiveness of MTSC based speed control.

articleTitle: Abuse Reporting System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: This project embarks on the development of an abuse reporting system designed to maintain user anonymity and employ advanced machine learning algorithms for genuineness assessment and fraud detection. In the contemporary digital landscape, safeguarding user privacy and ensuring the reliability of abuse reports are paramount. Our project addresses this challenge by integrating state-of-the-art machine learning techniques, enhancing the accuracy and efficiency of abuse reporting process, and mitigating false or malicious reporting. The technical underpinnings of the system involve the creation of a distributed, scalable, and fault-tolerant architecture capable of handling a wide range of abuse reports from diverse sources. We implement advanced natural language processing (NLP) models for textbased report analysis, while image and multimedia reports undergo deep learning-based content analysis. Anonymity preser-vation is achieved through advanced encryption techniques and decentralized data storage. Furthermore, we integrate adaptive machine learning algorithms that continuously evolve to detect novel abuse patterns and emerging fraud strategies, ensuring the system's adaptability to evolving threats. The project includes a comprehensive evaluation of the abuse reporting app's performance, precision, and scalability in handling a large volume of reports while preserving user anonymity. This project represents a significant advancement in the field of abuse reporting systems, offering a technologically robust and privacy-centric solution for contemporary society's increasing demand for secure and effective reporting mechanisms.

articleTitle: Real-Time House Price Predictions with Regression Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: Accurate property assessment is essential in the dynamic and ever-changing world of real estate so that both buyers and sellers can make well-informed choices. We are aware that setting the appropriate asking price for a house can be a difficult undertaking. Property values are greatly influenced by factors including location, size, amenities, market trends, and numerous economic indicators. This system supports in determining a property's price based on geographic regions factors, the number of bathrooms, bedrooms, and area (square feet). Forecasting future costs relies on examining historical market trends and value ranges. The primary focus of this analysis is to efficiently utilize regression models in combination with other methodologies to achieve the highest possible accuracy in predictions. This study aims to forecast housing values in Bangalore. Our website is designed to give you reliable and data-driven insights on property values when you're a potential homebuyer looking to identify the best property.

Index Terms: Least Absolute Shrinkage And Selection Operator

articleTitle: Power Quality Analyzer for Grid Connected Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: Interest in photovoltaic (PV) energy has surged due to its clean, inexhaustible nature, offering a pollution-free energy source. However, the process of converting solar energy into electricity requires an inverter to change direct current to alternating current. Unfortunately, this critical component, while adjusting AC power frequency, introduces issues that can compromise power system stability. Specifically, the inverter's switching nature can generate harmonics, distorting waveforms and potentially disrupting electronic devices powered by it, leading to malfunctions. This project studies harmonic characteristics within the grid, PV systems, and various loads. The findings could reveal the significant impact on grid harmonics caused by PV systems and loads when the inverter approaches its rated power capacity. Conversely, there's a reduction in harmonic percentages, and the type of load significantly influences the harmonics it generates. Additionally, upon comparing harmonics across the three aspects-PV systems, loads, and the grid-it becomes evident that the PV system's harmonics have minimal influence on loads, while loads significantly affect grid harmonics compared to PV systems. Our project aims to measure voltage and current with high voltage differntial probe (HVDP) and hall effect sensor respectively. With the measured voltage and current we aim to calculate the power quality by computing Total Harmonic Distortion (THD), Power Factor, frequency, and other parameters. For this we use fourier analysis which is done with the help of a microcontroller and display is used to output the measured values. In this phase we generated a PCB schematic for HVDP and BMS and tested the accuracy of the generated schematics using LTspice software. We also developed the chassis for our power quality analyzer and BMS. Now we focus in the implementation of display using microcontroller.

articleTitle: Autonomous Vehicles: A Breakthrough Towards Upcoming Multimedia Technologies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: With the advancement in technologies in terms of sensors, various multimedia devices are used in intelligent vehicles, and people are gaining interest in Intelligent Transport Systems (ITS). A smart city development includes smart transportation and ITS plays an important role in it. Autonomous Vehicle is one of the significant inventions of this framework. Autonomous Vehicles (AV) technology focuses on the improvement of transportation in terms of developing a highly accurate model which reduces congestion costs, reduces road accidents, also minimizes climate change effects by reducing the usage of Carbon and using green energy. In this paper, the focus is made on two multimedia technologies for the improvement of autonomous vehicles which are: collision prevention and path prediction. Both of the technologies need close human-computer interacting skills to fulfill the AVs requirement. In conclusion, this paper discusses various approaches related to the selected technology.

articleTitle: High Gain Buck Boost Converter with Single Switch and Low Voltage Stress
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: High gain DC converters are now necessary for photovoltaic (PV) energy sources. Lower efficiency and increased voltage stress are the outcomes of a conventional boost converter operating at a high duty ratio. With a lower duty ratio and less voltage stress, the suggested converter is made for high gain. Changing the structure's back-end voltage multiplier cell-which is modeled after the conventional buck boost converter-reduces the voltage stress on the switches. It is therefore possible to use low voltage rated switches. High conversion efficiency, wide voltage conversion range, and continuous input current characterize the high gain buck boost DC-DC converter. This converter meets all the specifications needed for a DC-DC converter used in photovoltaic systems. A comprehensive analysis has been conducted on the converter's operating principles and steady state properties. Simulated results were obtained using MATLAB / SIMULINK R2017b. The simulation's findings demonstrate the DC-DC converters' high voltage gain, high efficiency, and versatility in a variety of conversion scenarios. The microcontroller TMS320F28027F manages the converter. The theoretical considerations and simulation results derived from the prototype converter are confirmed by the experimental outcomes. The results demonstrate the wide range of conversion applications that can benefit from the use of a DC converter with high voltage gain, high efficiency, and low component stress.

articleTitle: Trapezoidal PWM Scheme for Selective Harmonic Elimination in Multilevel Inverters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: In this paper, an adaptive strategy for multi-carrier pulse width modulation (PWM) is introduced for selective harmonic elimination (SHE) in multilevel inverters (MLIs). Switching angles for harmonic elimination are chosen, and a reference wave is generated for each switching angle for a wide range of modulation indices. A single-phase cascaded H-bridge inverter is selected, and the multi-carrier PWM with the generated reference is implemented. Then the results are compared with conventional multi-carrier PWM strategies and with the standard selective harmonic elimination technique. Conventional SHE provided an average THD value of 38.5% while the proposed method was observed to give a better and reduced harmonic response with an average THD of 9.03% in the modulation index range of 0.3-0.75.

articleTitle: Vibration Assisted Impurity Detection in Liquids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: Vibration assisted impurity detection in liquids is a valuable technique for detecting and identifying impurities in a variety of applications. There are several ways that this technique can be implemented, including the use of piezoelectric sensors and resonant sensors. One key advantage of vibration assisted impurity detection is its ability to detect impurities at very low concentrations, making it an effective tool for ensuring the purity and quality of liquids in a range of industries. Viscosity of a liquid changes with the amount of impurity present within the liquid. Vibrational parameters such as frequency and damping time of mechanical structures that are immersed in liquids also change with viscosity. By taking these two principles, a methodology is formulated by constructing an experimental setup involving single degree of freedom mechanical vibrations damped by liquid. The frequency response and damping time of spring-mass system is analyzed to develop a correlation between the impurity content and vibrational characteristics. The vibration of spring-mass system immersed in a liquid is analyzed using an ADXL335 accelerometer for different compositions of liquid-impurity mixture.

articleTitle: CUNet: A Customized U-Net Variant Exploiting Convolutional Shortcuts
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: In recent years, across a range of computer vision tasks, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have demonstrated exceptional efficacy. Among these, image denoising stands out as a prominent application where CNNs have shown remarkable success. This study introduces a novel architecture called Customized U-Net (CUNet), tailored specifically for denoising tasks. It incorporates convolutional short connections and identity blocks within the U-Net framework in order to strengthen performance. The inclusion of the identity block reduces spatial information loss and enhances overall performance. To tackle the issue of vanishing gradients and accelerate the learning process, a ResBlock has been incorporated. For denoising process, the prior knowledge of noise level is not mandatory for this concept. Instead, it is trained using the BSD500 dataset to effectively address Additive White Gaussian Noise(WGN), encompassing a diverse range of noise levels <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\sigma)$</tex>. Experiments are conducted on different datasets such as CBSD68, Kodak24 and McMaster to quantify the performance of the model by calculating PSNR and SSIM. The performance, computational complexity and number of parameters of the CUNet is studied and compared with the performance of RDUNet. The results demonstrate slight improvement in the quality of denoised images while using fewer parameters and exhibiting reduced computational complexity and number of parameters compared to RDUNet.

articleTitle: Design of a Computationally Efficient 1-D Convolutional Neural Network Hardware for ECG Classification in Portable Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: Even though several machine learning techniques already exists for classification of Electrocardiogram (ECG) signals, most of them are less resource efficient for a viable incorporation inside a portable device especially wearable medical device. This paper proposes a computationally efficient 1-D convolutional neural network (CNN) with global maxpooling layer, which is able to classify the ECG signals with an accuracy of 98.26 % while the number of parameters is reduced by 62%, when compared to the latest existing work. A fully pipelined hardware architecture is also proposed for the implementation of this 1-D CNN structure. The synthesis results on field programmable gate array (FPGA) platform shows the resource efficiency of the proposed hardware over the other CNN architectures for ECG classification.

articleTitle: Wide Voltage Ratio DC-DC Converter for Ultracapacitor Charging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: A bidirectional wide voltage ratio converter is pro-posed in this paper for charging ultracapacitor banks from renewable energy sources for EV applications. The converter can perform buck and boost operations in both directions. The ability to work in buck and boost allows the system to work at any voltage level irrespective of input voltage. The coupling of the inductors in the converter reduces the ripple in inductor currents significantly, reducing either the inductor's size or the overall losses in the converter. A comprehensive analysis of the steady-state operation, effects of coupling, and effect parasitic resistances on the output voltage of the proposed converter operating in a continuous conduction mode is given. Through the study of the effects of parasitic resistances, the wide voltage ratio capability of the converter is verified. Small signal modelling is done, and the compensator is designed for constant current operation. Converter designed for a 500W power and tested in MATLAB Simulink for open loop and closed loop testing.

articleTitle: Estimation of Graph Parameters Using Graph Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: The paper addresses the potential of deep learning neural network architectures in estimating parameters of a graph. We considered two parameters namely complementary distance pattern uniform (CDPU) number and Kappa. A graph <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G =(V, E)$</tex> is a complementary distance pattern uniform (CDPU), if there exists <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M\subset V(G)$</tex> such that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f_{M}(u)=\{d(u, v)$</tex>: <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$v\in M\}$</tex>, for every <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$u\in V(G)-M$</tex>, is independent of the choice of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$u\in V(G)-M$</tex> and the set <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$M$</tex> is called the CDPU set. The least cardinality of CDPU set in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex> is called the CDPU number of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G$</tex>, denoted by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sigma(G)$</tex>. The vertex connectivity, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\kappa(G)$</tex> of a graph <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{G}$</tex>, is the minimum size of a vertex cut. Graph neural networks are widely used nowadays to solve numerous problems in science, engineering and social domain. Graph convolutinal neural networks (GCN) have been employed to estimate CDPU number and vertex connectivity of a graph. The results show the promise of recent deep learning architectures in estimating parameters of a graph.

articleTitle: Arduino Based Automatic Synchronizer for Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: This paper presents an Arduino based automatic synchronizer designed for microgrids, aiming to enhance the synchronization process in distributed power generation systems. The proposed system utilizes Arduino as the central control unit to monitor and synchronize multiple generators within the microgrid. Real time measurements of frequency, phase angle, and voltage deviations across the microgrid components are obtained using ZMPT101B voltage sensors, enabling accurate synchronization. The system incorporates an intelligent synchronization algorithm implemented on the Arduino controllers. To establish or break the connection between the generators and the microgrid, a three phase solidstate relay is utilized, eliminating the need for mechanical contacts and ensuring seamless synchronization. By continuously monitoring and adjusting generator parameters, the synchronizer enables smooth power transfer, minimizes disturbances and ensuring stable microgrid operation. The Arduino based automatic synchronizer offers a cost-effective and scalable solution for integrating renewable energy sources into microgrids. The utilization of Arduino microcontrollers, along with ZMPT101B voltage sensors and solid-state relay, contributes to improved synchronization precision, faster switching speed, reduced maintenance requirements, and enhanced overall system performance.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Models in Hand-Drawn Circuit Components Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: This study closely examines four major machine learning models with diverse architectures for their application in detecting electronic components within hand-drawn circuits. Pre-existing checkpoints of models were used for further domain specific training on custom dataset of hand drawn circuit images using Transfer Learning. The models under investigation include MobileNet SSD, YOLOv5xu, YOLOv8, and DETR transformer. For training, custom image dataset of 480 images with 1200 unique labels across 5 classes was generated. Inferencing and testing was performed on all models. Testing the power and efficiency of each model involves examining their approach to interpreting intricate hand-drawn diagrams. Various circuit designs, ranging from simple to complex, have been employed in these evaluations. The objective is to ascertain the strengths and limitations of each model through a comprehensive analysis of technical metrics. Such insights can aid practitioners in the field of Object Detection in selecting the most suitable methodology for their endeavors. Additionally, this paper proposes several enhancements to current techniques for identifying components within hand-drawn circuits

articleTitle: Fault Analysis of Inter-Turn Short Circuit of Switched Reluctance Motor for EV Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: Switched Reluctance Motor (SRM) is a best candidate for propelling an Electric Vehicle (EV) because of its simple and rugged construction, and most importantly due to the absence of permanent magnets. Even though these motors are fault tolerant in terms of motor-body fault, they are subjected to inter-turn fault. Diagnosis of this fault is very much important for reliable operation of SRM. This paper discusses the fault analysis techniques for the diagnosis of inter-turn fault. The mathematical modeling of a 6 phase, 12/10 pole, 850 W, 72 V, 9600 rpm SRM has been formulated. Two types of fault analysis techniques are mainly discussed (i) Partially shorting one phase winding (ii) By injecting a high frequency voltage signal to the non-operating phase. In first type, different scenarios including one-pole fault and two-pole fault are analyzed to study the effect on the motor parameters especially on the flux density distribution and on the motor inductance. In the second type, effect of adding a high frequency voltage signal in the phase current is analyzed. Finite element analysis (FEA) using ANSYS Maxwell is used to analyze these fault techniques, and the simulation results are presented. These techniques shall be utilized in the detection and diagnosis of the inter-turn fault in SRM.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence driven Portfolio Management
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: In general, portfolio optimization is used to strategically allocate funds into financial assets with the goal of maximizing returns over risk. In the traditional sense, such procedures necessitate a great deal of experience and rely on a trial-and-error approach. To address such inherent issues, this study provides a computational framework for integrating Monte-Carlo simulation-driven stock price optimization coupled with deep learning-driven forecasting of future stock prices. The Monte-Carlo simulation (MCS) is utilized to quantify the uncertain variations in the optimal parameters such as Sharpe ratio and volatility. The time history of the stock prices corresponding to the best stock (based on high returns over minimal risk) identified by MCS is further used to train the LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory) deep learning model. To ensure sound prediction capability, the constructed LSTM model is validated with out-of-fold unknown temporal history data. The presented coupled framework resulted in a promising method of portfolio management.

articleTitle: Transmitter Side Control in Wireless Power Transfer for Drone Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) technology has emerged as a promising solution for extending the flight time and operational range of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs), commonly known as drones. The effectiveness of WPT systems in drone applications heavily relies on maintaining a stable and constant output current despite variations in mutual inductance between the transmitter and receiver coils. when in constant current charging, the load variation effect on the current gain is negligible, and the effect of change in mutual inductance is very high when operated at resonant frequency of the system. Due to this issue the effect of mutual inductance needs to be addressed and necessary control action has to be taken to get the desired output. A method is proposed in this paper to addresses the critical issue of mutual inductance variation and to estimate the mutual inductance with the primary side information without any use of communication devices and ensure constant current delivery to drone batteries.

articleTitle: Improving Image Security through Data Concealment Methods Added with Arnold Transformation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: In spite of advancements in digital communications, the challenge of securing reliable data protection and safeguarding the exchange of confidential information persists. The least significant bit (LSB) method is favoured in steganography for its straightforwardness and user-friendliness. Nonetheless, its simplicity also makes it vulnerable to decoding, potentially exposing secret messages to unauthorised interception. This study introduces a hybrid approach that incorporates a revised version of the Collatz Conjecture with the Diffie-Hellman Key Exchange and the Arnold transform to create distinctive random sequences. The simulation outcomes, derived from certain datasets, resulted in average values of Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) and Structural Similarity Index (SSIM) of 80.24 and 0.9999, respectively. These results suggest that the suggested approach is highly efficient in creating stego-images that are almost imperceptible, using random numbers to select specific pixel locations for embedding the concealed message.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Early Prediction of Epileptic Seizures Using EEG
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: Epilepsy marks as one of the most prevalent neurological conditions on a global statistics and its consequences are reflected as seizure. The brain might certainly be harmed by prolonged seizures. EEG has been determined to be the optimum method for detecting the majority of regularly occurring brain disorders. The EEG of individuals varies depending on the circumstances surrounding their health. The typical EEG-based diagnosis for brain disorders is manual and time demanding. The paper proposes a system for analyzing EEG signals and examine distinctive EEG patterns in an epileptic patient with the objective to classify among the various stages of epilepsy using deep learning algorithms. For the practical implication, user interface framework is deployed to showcase the epilepsy stage and give appropriate seizure warning.

articleTitle: A Vision Transformer Approach for Drowsiness Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: The usage of Vision Transformer (ViT) for drowsiness detection is being shown by our work, which uses its uncommon attention mechanisms to detemine complex spatial correlations in facial images. Our method achieves a high accuracy of 99.8%, surpassing traditional approaches similar to MobileNet V2. Our work utilized Driver Drrowsiness Detection(DDD) Dataset. The ViT's excellent performance is associated with its ability to learn detailed and complex patterns from facial features, which highlights its effectiveness in picture classification tasks and its ability to handle real-world issues related to driver safety. This work highlights the adaptability and power of ViT in enhancing the precision and trustworthiness of sleepiness detection or recognition systems, giving more opportunities for further developments in the future.

articleTitle: Leveraging Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) for Image Deblurring
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: This research presents a method for image deblurring using generative adversarial networks (GAN). Blurry images often lack detail and affect image quality. This work tackles this challenge by leveraging the power of GANs to recover sharp images from blurry images. The main task of this research is to design and implement an advanced GAN for image deblurring. The design concept combines growth and maintenance techniques, improving the ability to capture fine details and improving image quality. The project explores new ideas such as misconceptions, circularity and self-monitoring to improve reality. The experiments involved training the model on GoPro dataset of blurred-sharp image pairs. The results showed a significant improvement in image deblurring compared to traditional methods. This project not only contributes to image processing, but also demonstrates the ability of GANs to solve real-world problems in image editing tasks. The detailed, architectures, and evaluations presented in this research provide insight into the performance and future directions of GAN-based image blurring agents.

articleTitle: An Ensemble Approach for Multiclass Classification and Optimization of Computational Time
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: This research centers on enhancing multiclass classification by introducing an innovative ensemble model. This model capitalizes on the strengths of decision trees with unique hyper parameters, offering a tailored approach to address the challenges of overfitting in machine learning. In practical testing on a Kaggle star classification dataset, our model attains a good accuracy of 97%, underscoring its effectiveness. Notably, our ensemble model strikes a harmonious balance between predictive performance and computational efficiency. This work contributes to the realm of machine learning, providing a valuable solution for multiclass classification tasks and showcasing the potential for practical application in diverse domains.

articleTitle: Facial Recognition and CCTV Integration for Enhanced Security Using Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence has resulted in significant progress in the realm of surveillance and security systems. This work delves into the potential of Multitask Cascaded Convolutional Networks (MTCNN), a face localization framework, coupled with FaceNet, a face recognition algorithm. The process involves real-time conversion of CCTV footage into frames, followed by the application of MTCNN to localize faces within these frames. Face coordinates are then extracted and transformed into embeddings using FaceNet. Subsequently, the K-Nearest Neighbors (K-NN) classifier, trained with a local database, categorizes these embeddings. This framework achieves precise detection and localization of individuals, indicating their presence within images through bounding boxes. This integrated framework is capable of detecting, tracking, and recognizing individuals across diverse lighting conditions and crowded environments. Additionally, the system contributes to criminal tracking and can help in lookout and missing person cases. The system also includes a user-friendly Graphical User Interface (GUI) for live monitoring of camera feeds and video footage. Moreover, the system presents the advantage of minimizing human resource requirements, thereby augmenting the operational efficiency of the surveillance system.

articleTitle: 3D Mapping of Indoor Empty Room Using 1D LiDAR
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: Three-dimensional mapping can be defined as the process of profiling of objects in three dimensions to map the object in real-world. The aim of the process is to create a 3D map of an object or a space which can be used in analysis, surveying, and other engineering domain. Among the available different approach of mapping the 3D mapping using LIDAR (Light Detection and Ranging) seems to be a promising method. The mapping using 3D Lidar is very expensive since the cost of 3D Lidar is high. The project proposed aims to develop a mapping technology by using one-dimensional LiDAR sensor to construct comprehensive 3D maps of indoor environment. Our approach leverages a single-dimensional LiDAR sensor, which offers a cost-effective and streamlined solution for creating detailed 3D maps of rooms and enclosed spaces. By employing advanced signal processing techniques, point cloud registration we aim to produce highly accurate and real-time 3D maps of rooms. These maps also capture the 3D structure of the architectural features within the space.

articleTitle: A Complex Network Analysis of the Youtube Video Network on Israel-Hamas War
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: It is important to analyze and understand the evolution of news, video, and other social media content during critical events such as a war. We created a new dataset and conducted a detailed study on the growth in the popularity of the videos published about the topic Israel-Hamas War on Youtube. Some of the existing studies have shown some bias in the Youtube recommendation algorithm, which influences the recommendation of video networks, thereby creating a dynamic network formed by recommended videos. To check for this bias, observe the evolution of the video recommender network, and study the recommendation algorithm, we conducted an analysis of the videos based on trending topics on Youtube. A new dataset was created based on the Youtube videos from the early days of war to the recent times. This dataset is used to analyze Youtube's recommendation algorithm and study how a video becomes popular. The study found that only a certain number of videos which are part of a giant component in the network became viral. When a video of a particular channel becomes popular, it is found to help the other videos of the same channel to get viral by forming a sub-component within itself.

articleTitle: Medicinal Plants Identification Using Deep Learning: A Survey
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: Medicinal plant identification has shown great benefit from deep learning, especially when CNNs are employed. CNNs are ideally suited for this task since they can extract complex features from photos. The promise of deep learning for medicinal plant identification is outlined in this research, which achieves up to 99% accuracy. This survey shows that deep learning can successfully detect medicinal plants in a variety of real-world contexts, such as open fields, rural places, and botanical gardens. Deep learning's ability to automate the identification process is a key benefit in this industry as it can assist alleviate the scarcity of knowledgeable and proficient botanists. Moreover, deep learning models can be implemented on mobile platforms, hence expanding their user base. This offers strong evidence that deep learning has potential applications in the recognition of medicinal plants. Deep learning models have the potential to aid in the building of an all-encompassing and dependable system for detecting medicinal plants in a variety of contexts with additional study and improvement.

articleTitle: SENet-based Diabetic Retinopathy Classification Using Data Augmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a common vision-compromising condition marked by retinal irregularities in individuals with diabetes. Precision in grading DR becomes challenging due to intra-class variations, the existence of minor lesions, and the uneven distribution of data. Diabetic retinopathy can be diagnosed using a dilated eye examination which is more time-consuming and needs an efficient ophthalmologist. Nevertheless, employing neural networks for image classification can help overcome these challenges. Traditional convolutional neural networks (CNNs) struggle to distinguish between small lesions. Furthermore, imbalanced data distribution can introduce bias to the model, favoring the more frequently sampled DR grades and thereby affecting the accuracy of grading. This paper aims to enhance DR grading performance by exploring the potential of various deep neural networks, with a specific focus on the Squeeze and Excitation model. We also introduce data augmentation techniques and compare their impact on model performance across different neural network architectures.

articleTitle: Automated Detection of Traffic Rule Violation using Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: The number of accidents on the road has increased as a result of more vehicles and less awareness among the populace. Motorcycle riders are involved in more deadly incidents than drivers of other types of vehicles. Many governments have mandated that motorbike riders wear helmets and follow traffic laws in order to limit the number of fatalities caused by accidents. The proposed system is intended to help law enforcement officials find motorbike riders who break traffic laws and also to raise awareness among them about the importance of following the rules. The system receives real-time traffic video and uses the Yolov5 model to identify objects in each frame. Based on a confidence score threshold, one of the frames featuring the motorcycle and the rider is chosen. The person's region of interest (ROI) is then used in a VGG16 classifier stage to determine whether the person is wearing a helmet or not. While a craft model is used to find the location of the licence plate from the motorcycle ROI. The identification of the licence plate aids the authorities in discovering the identity of the offender. A user interface is used to present the results of the classifier and text detection models to the user. The system exhibits an overall accuracy of 90 % when evaluated in a variety of scenarios.

articleTitle: Development of Deep Learning Model for Cardiac Arrhythmia Detection from ECG
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: An irregular heartbeat or abnormal cardiac rhythm is an arrhythmia. The heart can efficiently pump blood throughout the body when it beats regularly (rhythmic action). Early arrhythmia detection is crucial for avoiding problems, lowering risks, achieving better treatment results, and improving quality of life. Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) are important tools for detecting arrhythmias, especially when examining electrocardiogram (ECG) signals. In CNN, a Dense layer is used which is a simple layer of neurons in which each neuron receives input from all the neurons of the previous layer. This work explores the development of a deep-learning model for identifying arrhythmia using ECG signals. Since the older arrhythmia detection methods are not completely accurate and reliable, the testified CNN model can successfully detect and distinguish arrhythmia with a testing accuracy of 98.3% and a validation accuracy of 83.7% respectively. The counted testing losses were found to be 0.0542 and validation losses of 0.7764 in the range of 2. This model can effectively detect irregular heart rhythms at an early stage.

articleTitle: Development of Pneumatic Soft Gripper for Effective Material Handling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: Recent times have shown a drastic transition in robotics from rigid to soft mechanisms. The reason is that soft robots offer safer human-robot interactions, reduce weight and also offer strong environmental adaptability. However, the inherent characteristics of soft materials to exhibit multiple degrees of freedom (DoF) make it challenging to control their movements. Therefore, this paper presents the development of a soft gripper with simple architecture to effectively and economically manipulate delicate objects. The gripper constructed using silicon rubber has an air cavity to actuate its opening and closing pneumatically. This paper presents the different stages of its construction and demonstrates its application on a 4 DoF robotic arm for handling delicate objects. A simulation study of the structural parameters of the proposed soft gripper is also carried out using ANSYS finite element software. The preliminary results show the superior adaptability of the soft gripper in handling objects of various shapes and sizes. The proposed system can find application in food, biomedical and electronic industries.

articleTitle: AQUA - Water Management System at Home for a Sustainable World Using IoT
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: It is estimated that around 25% of the population do not have access to clean drinking water. Basically, our wasteful practices at home are a major reason for water scarcity. It's inevitable that we reduce water being wasted at homes for a sustainable future. Our proposed system “AQUA” can monitor and control the usage of water in residential areas through various sensors and actuators with the help of Internet of Things. The system is differentiated into various blocks for different areas within the building and they are controlled and monitored through a mobile application. There are mainly five sections: the Smart Plant Watering System implemented at the garden, the hand gesture shower implemented in bath areas, rain water harvesting system, water usage monitoring and billing and overflow prevention system which turns off tap automatically when water level reaches 90% of any container. By implementing the system at home, it was found that at least 10 litres of water could be saved per day per head. If this system is implemented in most homes across a town, in a year, at least few million litres of water could be saved.

articleTitle: Affordable Navigation Aid: A Smart Walking Stick for the Visually Impaired
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: An innovative effort to improve mobility and freedom is the Low-Cost Smart Walking Stick, which is intended for those with vision impairments. This inventive walking stick offers an effective navigation solution for a variety of locations by integrating affordable technologies like the ESP8266, ultrasonic sensor, buzzer, and vibrator. Users are greatly enhanced by being instantly notified about barriers, changes in topography, and potential risks through real-time notifications and haptic feedback. With the help of this affordable smart walking stick, people who are blind or visually impaired can now confidently and independently traverse their daily lives. It is a major technological advancement.

articleTitle: Comparison and Analysis of Various MPPT Controller Algorithms for DC-DC Converter in Solar Photovoltaic System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: Photovoltaic systems play a crucial role in harnessing renewable energy. This project focuses on the performance evaluation of a solar photovoltaic (PV) system employing a boost converter for Maximum PowerPoint Tracking (MPPT). The MPPT control is implemented using Perturb and Observe (P&O), Artificial Neural Network (ANN) and Fuzzy Logic Controller (FLC). The aim is to analyze and compare the performance of P&O, ANN and FLC in optimizing the energy extraction from the solar panels. These algorithms are employed to adaptively adjust the boost converter's operating point to maximize power output under varying environmental conditions. Through comprehensive simulations and experiments, this study evaluates the efficiency and effectiveness of the two control strategies, providing insights into their respective advantages and limitations. The results contribute to the understanding of MPPT techniques in solar energy systems, aiding the development of more efficient and adaptive renewable energy technologies.

articleTitle: Approximate 5–2 Compressors for Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: In VLSI architecture, the most preferable require-ment are area, power and speed efficiency. Approximate computing units have proved to become a promising and viable approach in achieving low-power design in error tolerable applications. In this paper, four new models of approximate 5:2 compressors are proposed. Three of them are developed using three different 4:2 approximate compressors from previous work along with the improved structure of full adder. The fourth model is designed using a parallel combination of half adders and full adder which reduces the delay to a great extent. The proposed 5:2 approximate compressors are compared with four existing designs. The proposed models give better PDP when compared with some existing approximate 5–2 compressors. There is an improvement by 56%, 61 %, 64% and 75% when the exact structure is compared with the proposed models Ml, M2, M3 and M4 respectively. There is an improvement in the error metrics when compared with the existing designs. All the approximate 5–2 compressors are designed using Verilog and synthesised using Cadence, genus tool in 90nm technology node.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Machine Learning Algorithms and Explainable AI for Fitness Club Attendance Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: The growing interest in health and fitness has resulted in an increase in the number of people joining fitness clubs. However, maintaining member engagement remains a challenge for fitness club operators. The goal of this study is to create a binary classification model that predicts whether a member is likely to attend a fitness club or not. In this paper, we propose a framework to explain how good the fitness club attendance classification performance will be under various Machine learning models by understanding its metrics. In this study by employing several classification models to determine Fitness Club attendance Classification using machine learning algorithms such as Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, Light GBM, etc. The Random Forest classifier performs with a higher accuracy of 0.87, and Explainable AI has been used to reveal the most significant feature.

articleTitle: AR Based Educational App: A Survey
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: Augmented reality is opening up exciting new frontiers in education by seamlessly blending digital enhancements with the physical learning environment. This fusion of real and virtual creates immersive experiences where abstract concepts spring to life. Students are empowered to actively construct knowledge and collaboratively solve problems within authentic contexts.AR enables 3D visualizations that overlay physical objects, allowing learners to interact with content in entirely new ways. Detailed computer graphics respond in real-time, transforming static materials into dynamic learning tools. Educators are leveraging AR's visualization and simulation capabilities to boost engagement and deepen understanding of complex topics. This emerging technology aligns well with constructivist and situated learning theories that emphasize hands-on, contextualized learning. By leveraging mobile devices, AR makes these powerful experiences available anytime, anywhere. The educational AR market is projected to grow exponentially in the coming years, reflecting the tremendous potential of this technology to reimagine teaching and learning. Educators are increasingly embracing AR to spark curiosity,promote active inquiry and create immersive digital layers that bring the classroom to life. This fusion of cutting-edge technology with pedagogical innovation points to an exciting future for augmented learning.

articleTitle: Implementation of Lumpy Skin Disease Detection Using Machine Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: Lumpy skin disease (LSD), a contagious ailment that can swiftly disseminate within cattle populations, presents a serious risk to the cattle industry's finances. Timely identification and precise recognition of afflicted animals are imperative to impede the transmission of the infection and mitigate its impact. Cattle and buffalo are the primary hosts of this viral malady, underscoring the urgency of effective measures. It is important to note that there is no health danger associated with LSD, however, it can seriously impair the welfare of animals and reduce output. Images are preprocessed using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) in order to extract features. The next step we will take is to use machine learning models such as Inception V3. Accuracy in identifying cow lumpy skin disease may be significantly increased by utilizing several machine learning methods. We have used total five machine learning models and calculated performance metrics for each model to determine how well models can work. Consequently, Inception V3 outperformed the other models, achieving 97.4% accuracy and 98.1% precision.

articleTitle: VisQAid: Visual Question Answering for Visually Impaired
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: Visual Question Answering for the visually impaired is an emerging and important research area. This field centers on creating technologies so visually impaired people can interact with their surroundings and learn by asking questions about visual content. The goal is to empower them to gain greater independence through this technology.A Visual Question Answering system has been developed to assist visually impaired people in understanding visuals. Using the VizWiz dataset, the proposed model learns from pictures and questions asked by visually impaired people. By training the system with Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training on this data, it can now respond to many visual questions in plain language. The results of the project shows the performance of the Visual Question Answering (VQA) system on the VizWiz dataset.An accuracy rate of 72.9% shows the ability to answer visual questions from those who have sight challenges.

articleTitle: Enhanced YOLOv8- Driven Traffic Rule Violation Detection with ROS-Integrated Autonomous Drone Navigation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: Employing autonomous drones, an expanded per-spective of the traffic situation may be obtained, covering more terrain than the existing monitoring system that depends on stationary cameras. Drones may also navigate through challenging-to-reach locations and complicated terrain, giving a more ac-curate and comprehensive view of the violations of traffic laws that are taking place nearby. Drones equipped with path planning implemented using ROS and the ability to detect traffic violations can greatly surpass the existing surveillance system. Proposed drones can record live videos of traffic violations, which deep learning algorithms can process to pinpoint the exact offense. These drones can quickly and accurately identify a variety of traffic infractions, such as speeding, illegal parking, and careless driving, by utilizing deep learning algorithms which utilize the YOLOv8 algorithm.

articleTitle: Edge Analytics Enabled Acoustic Rain Gauge
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: Precise, low-cost, and low-power precipitation measuring devices are vital to weather forecasting. However, conventional methods often suffer from limitations in maintenance, accuracy, cost, and power consumption. In this work, we address this problem by proposing a non-mechanical acoustic rain gauge system that leverages low-power Internet of Things (IoT) devices and deep learning algorithms. Our proposed system offers a novel approach to rainfall estimation, utilizing acoustic principles to accurately measure precipitation while minimizing energy consumption. Our research contributes to advancing the field of meteorological monitoring by providing a cost-effective and energy-efficient solution for rainfall measurement, thus improving weather forecasting capabilities.

articleTitle: Real-Time Detection of Speed Breaker and Potholes Using Machine Learning for On-Road Drivers and Visually Impaired Persons
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: Well-maintained roads are vital to a country's economy as they provide essential transit routes. Potholes and speed breakers, on the other hand, seriously endanger drivers and reduce safety. Inadequate night vision, inaccurate speed breaker signage, and careless driving are among the causes of these risks. On uneven roads, vehicles with limited ground clearance are hazardous. To address this, we provide a tool that uses a Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) integrated into a machine learning method. With the help of an ESP32 GPS Speedometer, the device can identify potholes and bumps and sends the position information including speed, latitude, and longitude to a cloud database using WiFi. Additionally, it uses a speaker to deliver speech alerts. Furthermore, MATLAB's Bayesian Regularization improves suspension health and lessens driver fatigue. Our solution integrates voice alerts, GPS navigational systems, and RNNs to improve road safety.

articleTitle: CT Image Denoising using Autoencoder and Generative Adversarial Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: Denoising images plays an important role in analyzing medical images. CT images usually contain a lot of noise which would affect the diagnosis. This project focuses on denoising CT images for better understanding and enhancing the accuracy of medical diagnosis. Proposed an approach for CT image denoising utilizing Convolutional autoencoders and Generative adversarial networks. The architecture integrates an encoder-decoder for Autoencoders and Generative adversarial networks including a Generator for generating denoised images and a discriminator for identifying real and fake images generated by the networks. Experimental evaluations conducted on synthetic and real CT datasets showcase the model's efficiency. When tested, achieved a PSNR value of 74.2 for Autoencoders and a PSNR value of 54.03 for Generative adversarial networks. Simulation results demonstrate the performance of this proposed method for denoising CT images.

articleTitle: Intelligent Vehicle Headlamp System Using LED Matrix
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: The study focuses on advancing automotive head-lamp technology, prioritizing safety and adaptability beyond traditional lighting functions. The key goal is to implement dynamic light control, intelligently adjusting headlamp illumination based on the proximity and direction of other vehicles to minimize glare for oncoming drivers. Additional safety features include automatic fog lamp activation through a humidity sensor, adaptive curve/side lighting synchronized with steering input, and environment-responsive intensity adjustment for optimal illumination in varying ambient lighting conditions. The integration of a Bluetooth module allows users to customize Daytime Running Light (DRL) patterns, aligning with user-centric automotive technology trends. Successful simulation using a Light Dependent Resistor (LDR) validates the feasibility of the dynamic light control mechanism, instilling confidence for the upcoming practical implementation phase. The study aims to significantly impact road safety and driving experiences by seamlessly integrating various components into an intelligent and cohesive headlamp system.

articleTitle: Modified Active Switched Network Based Novel Quadratic Gain Converter with Reduced Component Count and Voltage Stress
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: The demand for high-performance DC-DC converters with substantial gain is consistently growing, especially in the electric transportation, renewable energy, defence, and space applications industries. This manuscript presents a novel, modified architecture for a high-gain DC-DC converter in the active-switched network segment evolved from a conventional structure reported in the literature. Compared to the conventional design, the proposed topology eliminates a diode and capacitor. Through the rearrangement of components, the voltage stress on capacitors and the current stress on switch S2 are reduced. The operational principles in continuous and discontinuous conduction modes are elaborated, along with outlining the boundary conditions. The design methodology of the Active Switched Network Quadratic Gain Converter (ASNQGC) is presented in addition to an exploration of voltage and current stress on components, and a thorough loss analysis. An experimental validation verifies the analytical claims, and a comprehensive comparison with the literature is performed to showcase the competency of the proposed converter.

articleTitle: Energy-Efficient LEACH Approach Employing SOM and K-Means
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: An ad hoc deployment of several wireless sensors is the basis of an infrastructure-less wireless network known as a wireless sensor network (WSN). These sensors are positioned in a spatially ordered manner with the intention of monitoring and gathering environmental data. Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) are designed to wirelessly transfer data about physical variables, such as temperature, humidity, and other environmental parame-ters, that are being monitored in real time. Numerous industries, such as as industrial automation, healthcare, agriculture, and environmental monitoring, use this technology. The architecture of Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) is restricted by limitations in energy, bandwidth, and computational power. Several routing protocols have been created to overcome these obstacles and enhance network efficiency. Some solutions to address these challenges are implementing energy efficient protocols,bandwidth management and processing capacity optimization. Here in this proposal there is a comparison of nearest neighbour based K-means and Self Organizing Map (SOM) clustering based on LEACH which is Low Energy Adaptive Clustering Hierarchy protocol. According to the results, LEACH with K-means per-forms better when taking into account the number of rounds and throughput, although LEACH with SOM uses less energy.

articleTitle: Enhancing Bank Locker Security through Multi-Layered Authentication and IoT Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: In the face of evolving security threats, financial institutions continuously seek innovative solutions to fortify the protection of valuable assets stored in bank lockers. This research explores a comprehensive approach to enhance bank locker security by integrating multiple layers of authentication and leveraging the Internet of Things (IoT). The proposed system incorporates fingerprint recognition, keypad password entry, one-time password (OTP) verification, and real-time image capture of unauthorized access attempts. Fingerprint recognition ensures biometric uniqueness, offering a secure and convenient means of locker access. The inclusion of keypad password entry adds an additional layer of security, requiring users to input a personalized code. OTP verification further strengthens the authentication process by dynamically generating time-sensitive codes, minimizing the risk of unauthorized access. The integration of IoT plays a pivotal role in augmenting security measures. In the event of an unauthorized access attempt, the system captures and transmits an image of the intruder to a designated manager's bot. This proactive alert system enables timely response and intervention. Additionally, the system maintains an access history log, providing an audit trail for security administrators to monitor and analyze locker usage patterns. The proposed multi-layered authentication system with IoT integration not only fortifies bank locker security but also offers a robust defence against emerging threats. This research contributes to the on-going efforts in developing advanced security frameworks for safeguarding financial assets, ultimately fostering greater confidence among customers in the banking sector.

articleTitle: Formation Acquisition of a Multi-Agent System with Nonholonomic Dynamic Model of Wheeled Mobile Robots Using Model Predictive Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: In this paper, the formation acquisition of multi-agent system with non-holonomic dynamic model of wheeled mobile robots (WMRs) is addressed using model predictive control (MPC). The strategy is to augment the formation keeping term taking into account the relative positions of all agents. The power of Hungarian algorithm is exploited to further reduce the control effort by minimising the path travelled by the overall multi-robotic system. Simulation is done for 3 different cases and it is found that the proposed control design satisfies the design objective of formation acquisition with reduced control effort.

articleTitle: Load Frequency Control Using Adaptive Sliding Mode Control for a Two Area Interconnected Power System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: For a two-area power system, a unique adaptive sliding mode-based load frequency control is suggested in this work. Turbines of the non-reheat type are used in the power system. Despite the presence of external load disturbances and system uncertainties, the control objective is to maintain the frequency deviation, tie-line power deviation and area control error within predetermined limits. The conventional sliding mode controller (SMC) in load frequency control of a two area system has the demerit of chattering problem. This will cause the mechanical actuators or components to deteriorate, which is not good for the system. This study proposes an adaptive sliding mode control with higher performance than the traditional SMC. The particle swarm optimization technique is used to fine-tune the control parameters. Extensive simulation studies have been used to validate the suggested method's potential.

articleTitle: A Configurable AES Implementation on FPGA for Secure 5G Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: Advancement in technology and computational power has paved path for data security challenges in 5G communication. Confidentiality and integrity of data plays a key role in 5G networks. 5G systems are employed with different security protocols to facilitate security in high speed wireless communication. Among the various security systems available, Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) is observed to have better throughput and hardware efficiency. AES is one of the popular cryptography algorithms with three variants namely, AES-128, AES-192 and AES-256, each of which offers different levels of security. In this paper we present a configurable architecture for implementing the three variants of AES on hardware, so that the security level can be changed depending on the application. The proposed architecture has been implemented on Xilinx Virtex Ultrascale FPGA with an operating frequency of 175 MHz. The implementation results have been analyzed in terms of latency and hardware utilization.

articleTitle: Generative AI-Driven Automation of Business Process ReImagination
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: Traditional business process automation primarily concentrates on digitizing processes to achieve specific outcomes. However, it grapples with challenges stemming from manual configurations and inflexible workflows, restricting adaptability and creativity. This paper delves into the transformative potential of Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) in revolutionizing process automation, addressing the limitations inherent in traditional approaches. In contrast to traditional automation, Generative AI adopts a groundbreaking approach by harnessing data from past automation solutions to identify more effective methods. This goes beyond conventional orchestration, dynamically integrating software components, automatically generating rules from historical automation solutions data, and seamlessly integrating external systems. Generative AI unlocks its potential through the analysis of past workflows, gaining insights into components, decisions, and sequences. This knowledge serves as the foundation for creating new, efficient processes based on user-described natural language, resulting in robust workflows and rules that assimilate lessons from past best practices and adapt as needed. This innovative approach signifies a notable departure from traditional constraints, paving the way for a future where business processes evolve dynamically, aligning with the efficiency demands of the ever-changing digital landscape.

articleTitle: A Survey on Video Anomaly Detection in Surveillance System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: Surveillance video anomaly detection is a challenging and important task that aims to identify unusual or suspicious events in video streams without human intervention. Anomaly detection can help enhance the security and safety of various critical infrastructure systems, such as football stadiums, and cricket stadiums. However, anomaly detection also faces many difficulties, such as the diversity and complexity of normal and abnormal behaviors, the lack of sufficient and consistent annotations, and the high computational cost of processing large-scale video data. In this survey, we review the recent advances and challenges of artificial intelligence techniques in surveillance video anomaly detection. We highlight the strengths and limitations of different techniques, such as deep learning, generative models, graph neural networks, and multiple instance learning. We conclude by providing some future research directions and open issues in this field.

articleTitle: IoT Based Smart Health Care ATM System to Improve Quality Life
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: The rapid evolution of the Internet of Things (IoT) has heralded a new era in healthcare, offering unprecedented opportunities to enhance patient care through precision medicine. This paper presents the design and implementation of an IoT-Based Integrated Smart Healthcare Monitoring System aimed at enabling precision medicine by leveraging the power of IoT technology. The system integrates a wide array of sensors and wearable devices to continuously monitor vital health parameters, providing a comprehensive, real-time overview of a patient's health status. Through advanced data acquisition, processing, and analysis techniques, coupled with secure, reliable communication networks, the system facilitates the delivery of personalized healthcare services, tailored to the individual needs of each patient. We discuss the architecture of the system, highlighting its main components: sensors and wearable devices for health monitoring, data acquisition systems, communication infrastructure, data analysis and management tools, and security protocols to ensure patient privacy and data protection. The application of this system in chronic disease management, remote patient monitoring, and predictive health analytics demonstrates its potential to significantly improve patient outcomes, reduce healthcare costs, and advance the practice of precision medicine. Challenges related to interoperability, scalability, data security, and user privacy are addressed, along with proposed solutions and best practices for overcoming these barriers. Case studies exemplify the system's impact on patient care and health management, underscoring the importance of IoT in transforming healthcare services. The paper concludes with a forward-looking perspective on the future directions of IoT in healthcare, emphasizing the role of emerging technologies and patient engagement in enhancing the efficacy of precision medicine. By integrating sophisticated IoT technologies into healthcare systems, we can unlock new possibilities for personalized treatment, early disease detection, and efficient health management, marking a significant step forward in the quest for optimal health outcomes and quality of life for individuals worldwide.

articleTitle: Holistic Prediction Model for Analyzing COVID-19 Severity in Patients with Comorbidities using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: The global impact of the COVID-19 pandemic has been profound, affecting both public health and the worldwide economy. While the majority of COVID-19 cases result in survival, there are unfortunate instances of severe outcomes. Identifying at-risk patients early and implementing preventative interventions are crucial for improving survival rates and reducing fatalities. In this study, we analyzed 10 Lakhs patient samples sourced from the Kaggle repository, featuring 60 distinct features. Various classification algorithms, including Decision Tree Clas-sifier (DTC), Random Forest Classifier (RFC), Gaussian Navies Bayes (GNB), and k-Nearest Neighbors (kNN), were employed for data analysis. The dataset underwent initial preprocessing using various techniques, and missing values were addressed through methods such as kNN Imputer, SMOTE, Nearmiss to achieve data balance. Experiments were conducted using twenty-one features related to comorbidity diseases, along with drugs, and fourteen specific features were identified as significant for predicting survival in COVID-19 patients. The results revealed unbalanced recall outcomes with 100% performance metrics for k=3 and 5 in DTC of both unbalanced and balanced. These findings emphasize the importance of early detection and intervention strategies in managing the severity of COVID-19 cases.

articleTitle: Survey on Personalized Voice Assistant
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: This survey reviews the current state of personalized voice assistant systems that utilize natural language processing, speech recognition, and AI techniques. It examines methodologies for developing intelligent assistants that can securely access local data, learn preferences, and control IoT devices via voice. The paper analyzes the capabilities, advantages, and limitations of existing voice assistant solutions. It also explores their integration with web technologies and discusses challenges like privacy, speech accuracy, and language modeling constraints. The goal is to provide an overview of personalized voice assistant technologies, their potential impact, and future research directions toward enabling seamless voice-based interactions.

articleTitle: Efficient Adder Designs for Realizing Addition Subset of RISC-V P-SIMD Instructions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: The widespread adoption of Internet of Things (IoT) and the rising deployment of data-driven applications at edge devices demand efficient hardware architectures with high computational capability. RISC-V, an open source, flexible and modular instruction set architecture (ISA) very well expedite the design and deployment of IoT based edge applications. All the architecture vendors, including RISC-V employ single instruction multiple data (SIMD) instructions to accelerate digital signal processing (DSP) operations for resource-constrained edge devices. One such extension that aids the processing of large amounts of data is the P-extension, which introduces packed-SIMD instructions oriented for DSP applications. This paper proposes a novel design model for the implementation of ADD/SUB instructions of P-extension. The proposed model relies on the concept of reusing 9-bit adders to realize higher order adders. Evaluations of these deisgns on Xilinx Artix-7 FPGA device shows that the proposed design incurs around 40% improvement in area against the standard element-wise SIMD addition.

articleTitle: Neural Networks Assisted Vigenère Cipher Encryption of Text
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: With the recent advent of the digital interface in our day-to-day life, internet usage for a variety of purposes such as bank transactions, social media, communication and cloud storage has risen exponentially. Since the internet is surfed worldwide, the odds of the data being exposed to cyber criminals are significantly high. This establishes a strong rationale for devising an automated framework for end-to-end encryption for securing the data. In the present study, we utilized the computational efficiency of long short-term memory (LSTM) networks to predict the accurate vigenère cipher. The synthetic dataset with 10000 samples consisting of the alphabetical plain text and corresponding Vigenère cipher based on the fixed key “KEY” is utilized to train, test and validate the deep learning model. The validation of the LSTM model depicted exceptional accuracy, which is further reflected while performing different experiments of encrypting the plain text in the final stage of this study.

articleTitle: Elastic Stack: A Comprehensive Overview
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: This document thoroughly explores the Elastic Stack, comprising Elasticsearch, Logstash, Kibana, and Beats, emphasizing its effectiveness in real-time data analysis, log handling, and visualization. It examines the essential components, architecture, and practical uses in different fields, offering in-depth technical insights into each element, integration methods, and practical examples. Readers will gain a comprehensive grasp of the Elastic Stack's capabilities and its application potential in various scenarios by the conclusion of this paper.

articleTitle: A Complex Network Analysis of the OPEC Crude Oil Trade Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: Quantification and analysis of global oil trade networks reveals deep insights into a nation's development and influence at a global scale. Further, it allows us to predict future trends and changes to adapt state policy as the crude oil market influences the balance of power among the developed and emerging economies alike as it is central for energy needs as well for industrial progress. In this paper we analyzed the crude oil export data from 2016 to 2022 from Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries and their allies (OPEC+) using complex networks in order to quantify and create a comparison metric between the exporting and importing nations to identify changes in the trade network. Our analysis revealed that that subsequent to the COVID-19 pandemic, even after sizable economic recovery, Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) is unable to maintain pre-pandemic levels of trade due to multiple factors such as the rise of the USA as the leading oil exporter [14] [15], global financial sanctions on Russian federation resulting in influx of discounted oil in the markets [16], shift of world towards renewable energy [17] etc. As entering 2022 with the recovery of global oil trade the increase was 8.09% as compared to the loss of 12.35% on the onset of 2020. Our study also opens up possible research work in this direction about other major non-OPEC oil exporters and quantify how their control is increasing over the market.

articleTitle: IoT Based Intelligent Helmet for Miners
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: Utilizing Internet of Things (IoT) technology in the mining sector has the potential to transform safety protocols for workers, especially those from low-income backgrounds who may lack awareness of their rights. Given the substantial impact of the mining industry on a country's GDP, addressing safety concerns is urgent. The miner's helmet, a crucial element of their uniform, is essential for preventing head injuries in hazardous mining environments. Unfortunately, current practices often neglect worker well-being due to a lack of awareness. To tackle this issue, proposing the integration of diverse sensors into the miner's helmet takes a proactive stance. These sensors can monitor vital signs in real-time, providing crucial health data. Simultaneously, they can assess environmental conditions in mines, offering insights into potential safety risks. Additionally, incorporating a location-tracking solution ensures continuous monitoring of a miner's whereabouts, crucial for swift responses in emergencies. This approach reduces response times significantly, aiding in mitigating the impact of potential disasters. Embracing these technological advancements not only enhances worker safety but also showcases the mining industry's commitment to ethical practices and social responsibility.

articleTitle: Self Cleaning Solution For Solar Panel Utilizing Rainwater Harvester
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
