abstract: In the domain of sustainable energy solutions, a revolutionary way to solar panel maintenance has developed, seamlessly combining rainwater gathering, innovative roller mechanisms, and dual sun-wind power sources. This technique, which focuses on rainwater collecting and efficient cleaning, decreases the need for fresh water. It softly cleans panels while conserving energy and according to green energy standards. This novel approach not only saves resources, but also improves overall system efficiency.

articleTitle: Lithographic Hotspot Detection Using CNN
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: Reducing the feature size of semiconductor technology allows us to incorporate more functionalities in a single chip, making the fabrication more complex. The lithography process fabricates these tiny structures, creating desired structures with the help of masks to transfer the required patterns to the substrate. Due to the optical proximity of the commonly used fabrication method, the chances of occurrence of undesired patterns are high. These undesired patterns are called lithographic hotspots (HSs). Identifying these patterns before fabrication is crucial for fast semiconductor development. In this direction, an accurate HS detection method is proposed using the convolutional neural networks VGG16 and ResNet50. The proposed method shows improvements in performance measures compared to the existing techniques.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis by Machine Learning of Waste Biodiesels in CI Engine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: The escalating worries regarding environmental sustainability and the exhaustion of fossil fuel resources have sparked concerns and extensive exploration for substitute fuels for internal combustion engines are being conducted alternative fuels for internal combustion engines are being conducted. In the current investigation prophecy of engine and emissions performance on a CI Engine using waste fry biofuel was carried out, by utilizing cutting-edge Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) techniques. Experimental records from engine tests under diverse RPM and load condition are scrutinized with these algorithms. Various algorithms and training functions were employed to educate the models. The analysis establishes that waste fry biofuel has a momentous influence on engine performance, encompassing brake thermal efficiency and specific fuel consumption, while also diminishing detrimental emissions such as NOx (Nitrogen Oxides), smoke, and CO (Carbon Monoxide). ML and DL models aid in foretelling engine operation and emission control strategies, accentuating the potential of waste fry biofuel as a sustainable and environmentally friendly alternative to traditional diesel fuel.

articleTitle: Day and Night City View Image Translations Using Cycle GAN
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: CycleGAN, a type of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), is used in this study to tackle the difficult problem of translating cityscape photographs between day and night settings. Day-to-night picture translation is changing well-lit daytime images into nocturnal landscapes using artificial lighting, unique color palettes, and atmospheric effects, and vice versa. Previously, this work required labour-intensive manual involvement or specialised picture algorithms, but deep learning and GANs have introduced automation and better quality to this industry. CycleGAN excels at unpaired picture translation, even when there are no obvious correspondences between daylight and nighttime datasets. It makes use of the idea of cycle consistency to ensure proper translation between picture domains. This study focuses on training a CycleGAN model and found encouraging results. Beyond technical aspects, this paper highlights practical applications spanning film production, gaming, urban planning, traffic management, photography, environmental impact assessment, and more. CycleGAN's adaptability offers opportunities to enhance realism, aesthetics, and decision-making across various domains. In summary, this research underscores the potential of CycleGAN in day-to-night image translation, unlocking new possibilities in visualizing urban environments and influencing diverse industries and applications.

Author Keywords: Day and Night image translations using Cycle GAN

articleTitle: Airfoil Self Noise Prediction Using Machine Learning and Explainable AI
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: A major environmental challenge in the aerospace sector is presented by aircraft noise, particularly airfoil noise. Traditional methods for predicting airfoil noise involve complex and computationally intensive numerical simulations. This research explores the use of machine learning to enhance the efficiency and accuracy of airfoil noise prediction. By utilizing extensive datasets from wind tunnel experiments, encompassing a variety of airfoil geometries and flow conditions, supervised learning algorithms are employed to construct a predictive model. Diverse regression models, including random forests, support vector regression, CatBoost, XgBoost, Gradient Boosting and decision trees, are trained on the NACA 0012 airfoil dataset to uncover correlations between airfoil characteristics and noise emissions. Initial findings underscore the potential of machine learning, with Gradient Boosting regression achieving a noteworthy R2 score of 0.96625 and RMSE as 1.2622. This study not only equips engineers with a valuable tool for optimizing airfoil shapes to reduce noise but also establishes the groundwork for real-time noise prediction systems in aircraft operations.

articleTitle: Pest Detection and Disease Categorization in Tomato Crops using YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: This study introduces an innovative approach to enhance greenhouse management through the integration of YOLOv8, for the detection of pests and categorization of diseases in tomato crops. By amalgamating distinct datasets for pests and diseases, our research proposes a unified model capable of concurrently identifying and classifying these crucial factors that impact the health of tomato crops. The methodology involves the fusion of diverse datasets containing annotated images of tomato leaf diseases and pests to create a comprehensive training dataset for YOLOv8. Transfer learning techniques are employed to train the model, leveraging pre-existing knowledge embedded within the YOLOv8 architecture. The primary goal of the proposed model is to deliver accurate real-time detection. The results highlight the superior effectiveness of the YOLOv8 model compared to the YOLOv5 model in dual-purpose detection, demonstrating high accuracy and efficiency in identifying tomato leaf diseases and pests. Furthermore, the YOLOv8n model undergoes training and testing with various backbone architectures to reduce the number of layers and model complexity, and the results are compared with the default architecture.

articleTitle: MPPT Integrated High Gain DC-DC Converter for PV-fed Three Phase Induction Motor Drive
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: Induction motors are dominant driving horses in industrial drives due to their ease of control and low maintenance even though numerous types of highly efficient electrical motors are available in the market. The global energy demand is exponentially increasing day by day and still major share of the energy demand are met from the fossil fuels. The fossil fuels are diminishing very quickly in the natural reserve, hence adaption of renewable energy sources(RES) in power sector is happening rapidly. Solar Photovoltaic (PV) systems are best suited in this regard with low maintenance cost and environmental friendly operation. But the low voltage PV input is usually not enough to drive an high power induction motors in industrial applications. So a high gain DC-DC converter is unavoidable in these PV systems. These type of boost converters achieves the required level of output voltage. The Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) algorithm can also be integrated for the maximum utilisation of PV input. This paper presents an efficient PV-fed high gain DC-DC converter for a three-phase inverter of an induction motor drive. The PnO MPPT algorithm is used to control the input DC-DC converter. The simulation analysis shows this system can perform satisfactorily under variations in PV and load conditions.

articleTitle: Deep Fake Detection for Preventing Audio and Video Frauds Using Advanced Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: Deepfakes allow for the automated gen- eration of fake video content, often accomplished through the use of generative adversarial networks. To address the increasing issue of deepfakes, this study focuses on constructing a model that incorporates advanced techniques. The researchers combined the ResNeXt, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), and ResNet architectures, selecting them based on their effectiveness in handling complex visual data and capturing temporal dependencies. Prior to detection, the dataset underwent pre-processing using the Multi-Task Cascaded Convolutional Neural Network (MTCNN), which facilitated the accurate extraction of facial regions. Importantly, the study evaluated the model across three diverse and significant datasets: the Face Forensics++ dataset (FF-DF), the Celeb-DF dataset, and the Facebook Deepfake Detection Challenge (DFDC) dataset. This comprehensive evaluation en- sured the model's ability to generalize and its suitability for real-world scenarios, as demonstrated by its exceptional detection accuracy. The combination of models employed in this study yielded highly accurate results and remained robust in the face of evolving deepfake technology.

articleTitle: Sustainable Resource Allocation in Edge environment based on Deep Deterministic-Reinforced Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: Edge computing has the potential to revolutionise the speed and efficiency with which the information is processed particularly in real-time. Also, Edge settings are dynamic and comprise a wide range of elements, it is found effective handling multiple tasks at any instance. However, in such dynamic situations resource allocation is quite challenging. Resource allocation is expected to be optimistic and tamperproof so that the efficiency and performance of the overall edge computing environment shall not compromised. In this paper, an extensive study about resource allocation is carried and proposed a reinforcement learning based solution to effectively handle the dynamic resource allocation. The model uses a Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) is used to identify the need of resource allocation and apply the allocation strategies. The experiment is conducted using CRAWDAD KAIST - WIBRO dataset, which simulated the real workload and resources data. The obtained results are convincing, especially in terms of resource usage, response time, and energy efficiency.

articleTitle: Cricket Team Selection and Player Analysis using Data Analytics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: The inception of the “Cricket Team Selection and Player Analysis using Data Analytics” project arose from the imperative to introduce precision through data-driven methods in the process of selecting cricket teams. Recognizing the pivotal role of team composition in the sport, our project employs the K-means clustering algorithm to categorize players based on their historical performance data with the strike rate. This approach facilitates the streamlined creation of well-balanced teams, targeting cricket enthusiasts, coaches, and team selectors. The ultimate goal is to enhance their decision-making processes, optimizing team performance and strategy. The project adopts a comprehensive approach, heralding a new era in cricket by leveraging data. It enables the formation of playing elevens derived from historical player performance metrics, ensuring a more resilient and strategic selection process. The project also has a selection of top players based on the attributes provided by the user. The tangible outcome of this project is a tool designed to serve cricket stakeholders, aiding them in making informed decisions for improved performance on the field. Representing a significant stride towards a more data-driven approach to cricket, the “Cricket Team Selection and Player Analysis using Data Analytics” project is poised to redefine team selection and strategy in the sport. Its applicability extends to a broad audience, promising to be a transformative force in the realm of cricket decision-making.

articleTitle: Ensuring privacy of data in Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: Machine Learning is one of the most popular advancements in technology which is being widely used in various domains, including healthcare, avionics, automotive, business, education, etc. A Machine learning approach works by learning the required knowledge from the data to be supplied by a client system. In a typical scenario, a client entrusts a third-party agency to develop a machine learning application and shares the data to the developer to enable the development of a Machine learning application. This is badly affecting the privacy of data as a third-party is getting access to sensitive data from a client system. Therefore, an effective data encoding technique is required to ensure the privacy of sensitive data while enabling a third-party agency to develop a Machine learning application on the encoded data. Existing data masking/encoding techniques such as pseudonymization, anonymization and substitution are badly affecting the machine learning process as the modification they do for masking data is preventing a machine learning approach to learn the required knowledge. Another approach known in the literature is Fully Homomorphic Encryption. But, there is no tool available based on this technique which enables a client system to mask sensitive data before giving it to a third-party Machine Learning developer. We failed to obtain the expected outcome from an off-the-shelf Machine Learning classifier when we tried to classify a benchmark dataset masked using an available implementation of Fully Homomorphic Encryption. Since enough details about the implementation is not available, we could not find and fix the issues which is causing this problem. We propose a technique based on which we implemented a tool which provides an easy-to-use Graphical User Interface enabling the client to mask sensitive data before giving it to a third-party agency for developing a Machine Learning Application. Our tool enables a client to mask sensitive data through few mouse clicks. We mask sensitive data by applying a modified version of the RSA encryption system. We have applied our tool on three benchmark datasets and applied an off-the-shelf Machine Learning classifier on the datasets masked by our tool and found that the results obtained on the masked datasets are as good as the results obtained on the unmasked datasets.

articleTitle: Enhanced Image Registration for Precise Alignment of Brain and Liver CT Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: This study aims to assess improved methods of image registration to obtain accurate alignment of CT scans of the liver and brain. A collection of more than 1600 CT scans of the brain and liver is used in our research. We employ a variety of techniques, such as FFT-based registration with frequency domain analysis, Cv2 (OpenCV) for complete computer vision capabilities including picture alignment, and PystackReg, a Python package with a variety of registration algorithms. While Cv2 enables feature detection and geometric transformations, PystackReg offers a variety of transformation models. FFT uses spectral shifts to align images by taking advantage of frequency domains. By addressing particular aspects of the image, these techniques allow for accurate alignment of CT images throughout the registration process. As our CT dataset consists of two different anatomic data (Brain and Liver), we will divide the outcomes of each approach into two sections. To conclude our findings, we employ a variety of evaluation measures, including the Euclidean distance, Mean Square Error, Sum of Absolute Differences, and Jaccard Index. The FFT model is found to be more accurate in the dataset including brain CT scans, as evidenced by its higher Jaccard Index value (0.909) in comparison to the other models (0.439-PystackReg, 0.866-Cv2) and its lower Mean Square Error (0.090) in comparison to the other models (37.708-PystackReg, 0.130-Cv2). However, with the lowest Euclidean Measure (0.5974) and mean square error (0.0050) as compared to PystackReg (14.9810, 0.0386) and FFT (5.3996, 0.5727) models, respectively, the Cv2 Model performs better on liver CT images. These advancements could lead to better therapeutic evaluation, diagnostic capabilities, and personalized healthcare. They might also bring about a paradigm shift towards the analysis and interpretation of medical pictures that is more successful and efficient.

articleTitle: An Explainable AI Model for Student Engagement in Tablet Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: This study examines the effectiveness of tabletintegrated teaching and learning in rural India using artificial intelligence (AI) models. Academic motivation was assessed using the Instructional Materials Motivation Survey (IMMS) in the afterschool programs of seven centers located in Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh, Telangana, and Karnataka. The survey is based on the ARCS model for motivation, which postulates that the traits of academic motivation include Attention, Relevance, Confidence, and Satisfaction. The main research question is which of these components contributes the most to the successful participation of a student in the tablet-integrated teaching program, where participation is measured by tablet usage by the students. Our research utilized the AI model XGBoost to examine the trait of academic motivation to make predictions about the students’ participation in the program. The SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) algorithm enables the interpretation of the impact of traits on predictions, which is visually depicted using Waterfall and Beeswarm plots. These graphic explanations allow us to interpret the model's prediction. In that way, the explainable AI model helps to understand methods to improve confidence in students and to relate the connection between the relevance of any technologyintegrated academic intervention program and student attendance.

articleTitle: Enhancing Compressive Strength Prediction in Fiber Reinforced Geopolymer Concrete Through Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: This research focuses on accurately predicting the compressive strength of Fiber Reinforced Geopolymer Concrete (FRGC) using machine learning techniques, considering the material's complexity and diverse factors influencing its strength. A machine learning model was developed to forecast the compressive strength of FRGC, leveraging data analysis and comparison of regression techniques. Linear Regression, Lasso Regression, and Ridge Regression were assessed for their predictive accuracy. Feature selection methods were employed to identify influential factors impacting compressive strength. The Random Forest Regressor emerged as the most effective model, exhibiting the lowest Root Mean Square Error (RMSE). The findings offer a valuable tool for engineers to optimize FRGC properties, enhancing its strength and sustainability for various applications. This study underscores the potential of machine learning in streamlining material design processes in civil engineering.

Index Terms: Least Absolute Shrinkage And Selection Operator

articleTitle: A Deep Learning-Oriented Approach for Lung CT Augmentation: Leveraging U-Net and GAN Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: This study concerns the use of complex imaging methods like integrating ResNet, Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN), and U- Net with a single set of variables. Improving medical image analysis for lung-related diseases is the primary objective. This study performs in- depth analysis of lung CT data, aiming at improving UNet parameters, GANs and ResNet for better segmentation experience effects on 3D volume rendering images classification. The major effort here is tuning the parameters of the U-Net architecture, training GANs for generative tasks and applying ResNet to improve feature extraction and classification. To provide more detailed understanding of structures in the lung, advanced 3D visualization techniques are used to give greater insights into abnormalities. With the use of U-Net, GAN and ResNet together can classify lung CT scans. This provides a way to distinguish between general patterns and specific problems. The main goal is to fuse these solid building blocks in order to process medical pictures for better results, that will increase the effectiveness and accuracy of diagnosing diseases related with lungs.

articleTitle: Emotion Recognition in Speech: Conventional Test-Train Approach and Pseudo Transfer Learning Strategies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: Speech emotion recognition (SER) is a pivotal component of human-computer interaction. This research attempts to utilize Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC) to devise a transfer learning-like approach. Using a diverse set of machine and deep learning models, this work tries a two-phase evaluation methodology with which the robustness and generalization capabilities of the SER model are investigated. The pseudo-transfer learning approach is investigated over genders and languages and the results are summarized. The results and derived insights assert on the possibility of potential effective strategies that can substantially elevate the accuracy and robustness of emotion recognition systems.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Education in Emerging Markets: Understanding ChatGPT Adoption through a Comprehensive Lens of UTAUAT, Flow Theory, and Critical Mass Theory
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: The study's objective was to develop a model that examined the predictors of adoption and use of ChatGPT among graduate students. To understand the adoption of this novel technology, we modified the UTAUT2(Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology −2) model to include variables from critical mass theory and flow theory. The respondents were graduate students from remote locations in India, this is a unique contribution. The data was analyzed using PLS-SEM and it was found that effort expectancy, habit, performance expectancy, and personal innovativeness are significant drivers that motivate graduates to adopt ChatGPT.

articleTitle: Amazon Kindle Review Sentiment Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: In the digital age, the exponential growth of user-generated content, particularly in online platforms like the Kindle Store, has prompted the need for efficient sentiment analysis methods. This study explores sentiment analysis within Kindle Store book reviews using machine learning techniques to extract insights, aiding stakeholders in decision-making processes. Focusing on sentiment classification-positive, negative, or neutral-the research assesses the efficacy of Logistic Regression and Random Forest models in analyzing sentiments. Key preprocessing steps address data cleaning, noise reduction, and class imbalance, ensuring readiness for model training. Stakeholders, including authors, publishers, and readers, seek insights from sentiment analysis for marketing strategies, book reception evaluation, and informed book selection. The contemporary issue lies in automating sentiment analysis due to the vast volume of unstructured textual data, diverse sentiments, and the need for precise analysis. Challenges encompass diverse sentiments, varying review quality, absence of standardized structures, and biases in the data. The tasks involve data collection, annotation.feature extraction, model selection, evaluation, optimization, deployment, and iterative improvement. Successful completion of these tasks leads to a robust sentiment analysis framework for Kindle Store reviews, contributing to the discourse on sentiment analysis methodologies and their broader applications beyond e-commerce.

articleTitle: Vision Through Technology: ‘Digi Drishti's’ Pioneering Role in Assisting the Visually Impaired
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: The “Digi Drishti” project is a groundbreaking initiative in assistive technology designed to assist visually impaired individuals in public transportation systems. The project aims to bridge the gap between advanced technology and the practical needs of this demographic, enhancing their independence and quality of life. The core of the project is its innovative use of image processing and machine learning algorithms for currency recognition, which uses a highresolution camera and a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to accurately identify currency denominations. The device also integrates QR code scanning capabilities, providing real-time navigation assistance in public transportation. The design philosophy is user-centric, focusing on intuitive operation, reliability, and accessibility. The hardware architecture includes a Raspberry Pi microcontroller, a dual-camera module, and an audio output system, while the software architecture is a blend of operating systems, programming languages, and libraries. The development of “Digi Drishti” followed a structured and iterative approach, including conceptualization, design, implementation, and rigorous testing. The results have been overwhelmingly positive, with high accuracy rates in currency recognition and QR code scanning, even under challenging conditions. However, the project identified areas for improvement, such as enhancing performance in low-light conditions and refining the ergonomic design. “Digi Drishti” demonstrates the potential of technology to make a tangible difference in the lives of visually impaired individuals and demonstrates how innovative solutions can be developed by understanding and addressing specific challenges.

articleTitle: Cache Based Side-Channel Attacks: A Survey
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: This survey examines the diverse mitigation strategies that have been applied to the cloud infrastructure in order to fortify it against cache-based side-channel attacks. We categorizes strategies into: hypervisor-based, hardware-based, and two-stage defense methods. Different classifications provide unique approaches to mitigate these vulnerabilities. The study thoroughly examines their results, encompassing precision, efficiency, and potential ramifications for cloud systems. In addition, the survey examines the inter dependencies among these solutions, highlighting the necessity for operating system or hypervisor modifications to ensure optimal functionality. The study primarily focuses on analyzing the false-positive rates of these solutions. The survey's objective is to provide a thorough examination of cache-based side-channel attack defences, including their effectiveness, dependencies, and potential impact on cloud performance and security. To further enhance security, we additionally suggested countermeasures against these assaults.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Document Summarization: Examining Key Influences on the Adoption of ChatPDF for Enhanced Student Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: This study investigates how document summarization using ChatPDF, an online tool that uses the ChatGPT API, can improve student learning. The research examines the factors influencing ChatPDF uptake in educational situations and explores the body of work on document summarising by utilising the UTAUT paradigm. Key determinants such as Performance Expectancy (PE), Effort Expectancy (EE), Social Influence (SI), Facilitating Conditions (FC), and Behavioural Intention (BI) are established by the conceptual model given in the study, which is based on the UTAUT framework. Together, these factors influence the uptake of ChatPDF, and the analysis highlights important connections and interdependencies between them. The study highlights how important Effort Expectancy is in determining Facilitating Conditions and shows a substantial and statistically significant correlation. Moreover, the research reveals a clear relationship between Social Influence and Effort Expectancy, highlighting the significance of interpersonal aspects in the adoption of new technology. The study also highlights the role that Facilitating Conditions play in influencing Behavioural desire (BI), showing a strong positive correlation between improved conditions and students’ desire to use ChatPDF. According to the study, ChatPDF emerges as a disruptive force in contemporary education, providing students with a more effective and captivating means of navigating and understanding vast amounts of information by means of faster document summarising procedures. The study's findings support the use of these digital technologies in educational environments and present them as important tools for enhancing student learning.

articleTitle: IoT Attack Detection:Using Feature Selection and Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) is facing a growing concern regarding cyber-attacks and the need for anomaly detection. As the deployment of IoT devices rapidly expands, the number of attacks targeting these devices increases, posing a continuous threat of exploitation and danger. Various types of attacks, such as malicious operations, denial of service, MITM (Man-in-the-Middle), and scanning, can lead to the failure of IoT devices. In our study, we examine the effectiveness of several machine-learning algorithms, including decision trees, random forests, gradient-boosting machines (GBM), Support Vector Machines (SVM), Naive Bayes, Adaboost, and the unsupervised classifier K medoids. The objective is to analyze and predict network attacks targeting IoT devices. These algorithms are implemented in MATLAB platform. The dataset used here is IOTID2020 network intrusion dataset. The accuracy of the model by using adaboost is the highest that is 99.92% for normal and abnormal classification. The accuracy 99.49% for category classification.

articleTitle: A Review and Comprehensive Analysis of Recent Research in Crop Yield Prediction using Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: Traditional farming based on conventional methods has been the pillar of agricultural practices for a long time. But, due to the escalating global population, unstable climatic patterns and limited resources, the efficiency of traditional methods is facing challenges. The introduction of data-driven and artificial intelligence based approaches involving machine learning and deep learning have gained significant popularity capturing the interest of numerous researchers. This review examines various algorithms, including Random Forest, Decision Trees, K-Nearest Neighbours, Lasso Regression, Stacked Regression, and XGBoost, along with deep learning techniques like LSTM, RNN, and SVM. The study highlights their performance across multiple metrics such as accuracy, RMSE, MAE, R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, and MSE. Notably, Random Forest emerges as a highly effective model due to its excellent performance in accuracy, RMSE, MAE, and R2. Lasso Regression and XGBoost also show remarkable results in RMSE and MSE, respectively. Deep learning models like LSTM, RNN, and SVM are recognized for their high accuracy, underlining their potential in handling complex agricultural data. Through an examination of diverse approaches and data sources, this review seeks to explain and define the capabilities of these innovative technologies for sustainable agrarian applications.

Index Terms: Least Absolute Shrinkage And Selection Operator

articleTitle: VisualBlend - A Mixed Approach on Forensic Image Generation and Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: An extensive use case of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) that not only combines artistic creativity with technological innovation but also significantly improves identification precision, filling in critical gaps in the smooth integration of textual descriptions with visual representations. The motivation is rooted on the difficulties that currently exist in accurately identifying human face sketches by directly transforming them into images, an area where prior approaches were inadequate. Our special dual-function technology is designed to get beyond these obstacles and provides a fresh approach for forensic investigators, artists, and sculptors. It has the ability to convert text to image as well as sketch to image. This easy transformation of textual and drawing data represents an integrated combination of creativity and technology that is set to have an impact on a number of disciplines, such as suspect identification and crime scene reconstruction.

articleTitle: High Gain Dual Duty Stepup Triswitching Transformerless Converter for Stable High Voltage DC Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: This paper focuses on advancing high gain DC-DC converter for stable high voltage applications. The ATMEGA328P microcontroller is employed for precise voltage control, enabling real-time monitoring and adjustments to maintain a constant voltage level. The proposed approach integrates cutting edge power electronics with digital control, overcoming challenges in high-gain converter voltage stability while ensuring efficiency. The research explores potential applications in renewable energy systems, DC Micro-grids, and portable electronic devices with respect to the limitations of existing DC-DC converter topologies in terms of stable high voltage applications. Eventually, the best architecture is selected, and the boost converter topology with a feedback control loop is implemented. The paper delves into detailed design aspects, including component selection and algorithm development. Employing pulse width modulation, the implemented control algorithm efficiently drives the converter, achieving high voltage gains with low output voltage ripple and robust regulation. A 12/120V prototype circuit is developed and verified for performance validation.

articleTitle: Accelerating Native Inference Model Performance in Edge Devices using TensorRT
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: In this era, deep learning is becoming increasingly popular for solving real-world problems. Due to the extremely high processing power required to execute the most complex deep learning models, Graphics Processing Units(GPUs) and Neural Processing Units(NPUs) are essential for optimal execution. However, it is challenging to incorporate these high-performance processors in every edge device like Internet of Things gadgets, embedded systems, and cell phones to execute complex inference models. Hence, deep learning models must be optimized to perform well on edge devices with limited memory, power, and computing capabilities. Optimizing the inference models to accelerate performance on edge devices is one of the significant issues facing, especially in complex computation domains like computer vision. TensorRT, introduced by NVIDIA, is one of the best approaches used to optimize inference models, by accelerating their performance on edge devices without compromising the model accuracy. It presents a variety of optimization approaches, including layer fusion, quantization, dynamic tensor memory management, kernel auto tuning, and precision calibration. Every optimization technique is contingent upon the problem that have selected and the use of all optimization approaches has the potential to significantly speed up the performance of an inference model. This paper explores how TensorRT accelerates the performance of inference models like ResNet-50, VGG16, and Inception V3 in an image classification problem, and the results are analyzed with its native inference models. The utilization of TensorRT in edge devices is expanding significantly, reflecting a growing scope for enhanced performance and efficiency in processing complex neural networks at the edge.

articleTitle: Automated Short Answer Grading With Word Embedding-Based Semantic Similarity Using PySpark
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: Automated short answer grading, a pivotal advancement in educational assessment methodologies, addresses scalability challenges and streamlines evaluation processes using natural language processing and machine learning. This technology ensures timely, consistent, and objective feedback, replacing manual grading to mitigate biases and variations, thus enhancing the educational experience. The proposed model employs Word2Vec to generate word embeddings for each student response and the corresponding reference answer. By leveraging cosine similarity, the model calculates semantic similarity between the vectors, producing a score ranging from 0 to 1. This cosine similarity score is then scalable, allowing for the computation of final grades based on question-specific weightage, providing a robust and scalable approach for automated short-answer grading. In the context of this work, regression-based evaluation metrics yielded a Mean Squared Error (MSE) of 0.2727 & R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> score of 0.67, demonstrating the efficacy of the automated grading system in achieving accurate and reliable assessments.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Survey on Digitization in Restaurant Sector
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: In recent eras, the restaurant industry has undergone a significant transformation with the increasing use of technology. Digital Menu card is one such innovation with a booking, ordering, and recommendation system, which has a dining experience for customers. In the following system, customers can access the food menu digitally by placing the order from their device to the kitchen without involving waiter staff, and receive personalized recommendations based on their preferences. The digital menu card and ordering system have several merits, such as reducing wait times and improving order accuracy. The recommendation system, on the other hand, enhances the customer experience by providing recommendations based on their past orders, dietary restrictions, and other preferences. The implementation of this system also benefits the restaurant in terms of increased efficiency and reduced costs. With digital menus, the restaurant can update their offerings in real-time and eliminate printing costs. The ordering system streamlines the order taking process, reducing the need for additional staff during peak hours. Overall, the digital menu card with ordering and recommendation system is a pioneer for the restaurant industry, providing a seamless and personalized experience for customers while increasing efficiency and reducing costs for restaurants.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Hierarchical Attachment Process in Nested Network Mobility
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: The proliferation of mobile devices and the ever- increasing demand for seamless connectivity have driven the evolution of network architectures towards greater complexity. In this context, Nested Network Mobility (NeNEMO) has emerged as a promising paradigm to support the mobility of mobile network nodes (MNNs) across heterogeneous wireless networks, enabling continuous communication and optimal resource uti-lization. One critical aspect of NeNEMO is the hand-off process, which ensures that MNNs smoothly transition between different network domains. However, in this basic support protocol, the burden of tunneling overhead escalates with the nesting level of mobile networks. Regrettably, the majority of these protocols falter in delivering the requisite quality of service, particularly in highly nested network scenarios. This paper presents a novel approach to the hierarchical attachment process within a nested network mobility framework. This process provides explicit guidance to new mobile network nodes, directing them to attach at an optimal nesting level to enhance service quality. Our observations indicate that our proposed technique of mobile node attachment significantly ameliorates hand-off delay within the intricate scenario of network mobility in its nested mode.

articleTitle: Fault Detection using TinyML, Design and Control of Three-Phase Two-Level Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: The depletion of natural sources of mineral oil has led to a search for alternative sources, particularly in the transportation industry where electric vehicles (EVs) are gaining traction. However, current EV technology is still relatively primitive and requires significant improvements to ensure better and prolonged service. Efforts are underway to design and develop more efficient EV models, with a key focus on the powertrain. The powertrain, comprising the electric motor, power electronics, and transmission, is crucial for efficient energy conversion in EVs[1]–[2]. Through literature surveys and iterative processes, various parameters for Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (PMSM) based drives have been identified[4]. These parameters include electromagnetic speed, peak and RMS current, inductances (Ld, Lq), flux, inertia (J), resistance (Rs), damping coefficient (B), and pole pairs. The control strategy employed is Field Oriented Control (FOC), which encompasses Field-Weakening Control[7] and Maximum Torque Per Ampere (MTPA) as the operating regions. A three-phase 2-level inverter utilizing Space Vector Pulse Width Modulation (SVPWM)[5] for precise voltage control has been selected as the inverter of choice. This design also incorporates Insulated-Gate Bipolar Transistors (IGBTs) as switching devices, along with TinyML for comprehensive powertrain operation efficiency in EVs. The objective of this comprehensive design approach is to develop a three-phase two-level voltage source inverter with fault detection using TinyML (Edge Impulse) that optimizes the performance of electric vehicles to meet the growing demand for efficient transportation solutions.

articleTitle: A Review on Federated Learning with a Focus on Security and Privacy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) enables the collaborative training of a global model without centralizing data, effectively addressing privacy concerns in the field of machine learning. However, FL remains vulnerable to various security and privacy threats, such as adversarial attacks, data poisoning, and privacy inference. This paper provides a comprehensive analysis of these threats, categorizing them based on the attacking party (aggregator or participant). We review state-of-the-art mitigation techniques, highlighting blockchain and differential privacy. Finally, we identify promising research directions for securing and enhancing FL privacy. This paper serves as a reference for developing secure and privacy-preserving FL solutions.

articleTitle: Malayalam to English Named Entity Transliteration using Attention based BiLSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: This research introduces an approach to Malayalam-English named entity transliteration using a BiLSTM with attention mechanism and compares its perfromance with basic LSTM and BiLSTM frame-works. A selected subset of 27 million named entity parallel corpus is employed for training the translit-eration model. The trained model exhibits promising results, achieving an accuracy of 53% on a held-out test set, with an impressively low character error rate (CER) of 7.7%. Notably, our model demonstrates a high degree of generalization beyond named entities. In testing its capabilities on non-named entities. The character tokenizer applied in this model has shown surprising proficiency in transliterating regular words in Malayalam, including single morpheme words, as well as those with inflections and agglutinations. This research underscores the potential of utilizing spe-cialized parallel corpora for enhancing transliteration models. Furthermore, the flexibility of the proposed architecture allows for training reverse transliteration, converting English names to Malayalam script. The findings presented here contribute valuable insights to the broader domain of cross-language information processing and pave the way for future improvements in the transliteration of Indian languages.

articleTitle: Analyzing Farmers Suicides in India: A Comparative Study of Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: This study employs advanced Machine Learning (ML) algorithms to predict and analyze farmer suicides in India using a comprehensive Kaggle dataset spanning 2001 to 2012. When focusing on high accuracy, algorithms like Decision Trees and K Nearest Neighbors (KNN) perform better than others, with rates of 86.09% and 85.99%, respectively. The study emphasizes the potential of machine learning (ML) models in detecting crucial trends and variables that lead to farmer suicides. This provides insightful information for efficient policy interventions and focused approaches to deal with this serious issue.

articleTitle: Black Pepper Leaf Disease Classification using Deep Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: Black pepper crops are susceptible to various diseases, resulting in reduced yields. Different fungus can produce dark, sunken lesions on black pepper fruits, rendering them unmarketable. Powdery mildew, characterized by a white, powdery growth on the leaves, can hinder photosynthesis and reduce crop quality. To combat these diseases, farmers often employ cultural practices like crop rotation, proper irrigation, and disease-resistant black pepper varieties. They may also use fungicides and other chemical treatments as part of an integrated pest management strategy to mitigate the impact of these diseases. Timely identification and control of black pepper diseases are crucial for maintaining healthy plantations and ensuring a successful pepper harvest. The black pepper leaf disease classification study focuses to develop a robust system for identifying and categorizing leaf diseases in black pepper crops. Currently farmers manually identify these diseases, which requires more time and experience. There are no automated systems for this task. By leveraging advancements in AI and Deep Learning techniques and implementing new algorithms, we can identify these diseases more efficiently and quickly. An automated system that classifies these diseases faster can help to find solutions for their cure. The significance of this approach lies in its contribution to efficient disease management in black pepper crops. Better classification enables farmers to identify leaf diseases promptly and implement appropriate mitigation measures, leading to enhanced crop health and productivity. Overall the study emphasizes the effectiveness of black pepper leaf disease classification. The developed system provides a valuable tool for agricultural practitioners to make decisions and take proactive measures in disease management.

articleTitle: Construction Equipment Performance with Cloud Data Analysis for Predictive Maintenance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: The research uses Internet of Things technology for predictive maintenance in the construction sector. The system addresses incorporating Internet of Things sensors into construction machinery to enable real-time monitoring of operating parameters. The study suggests a proactive maintenance strategy that may anticipate equipment breakdowns by examining the data obtained and using sophisticated prediction models. With this strategy, construction teams can arrange maintenance activities systematically, which cuts down on downtime and helps avoid expensive interruptions. The abstract emphasizes the advantages of this practice, which include reducing unexpected downtime as much as possible, extending the life of equipment, and making the most of available resources. The study proves the usefulness of the IoT-based predictive maintenance approach via empirical investigations and the analysis of case studies. This validates the strategy's efficacy, contributing to enhanced equipment performance and increased work efficiency in the construction industry.

articleTitle: Visualizing Alzheimer's Prediction: An Ensembled Deep Learning and Grad-CAM Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: Alzheimer's Disease (AD) is a neurological disorder which is irreversible and progressive in nature. Deep Learning (DL) architectures have enhanced ability to detect and classify AD based on brain MRI images. For all that, as the DL models are black-box in nature, it is challenging to trust model's accuracy. Visualization techniques visually highlight the salient regions in the MR images that have been identified by the model for the classification task. In this study, we examine two pretrained deep learning networks-Inceptionnet V3 and EfficientN et B7, and propose an ensemble approach to classify the four stages of AD. In addition, we present Grad-CAM approach to visualize the aspects of AD disease and to gain insights into the model's perception in classifying the AD into the four categories. The results reveal that the ensembled approach achieved an impressive classification accuracy of 93%, surpassing other models and Grad-CAM could identify and discriminate the brain regions in the MRI images which are responsible for AD classification. Thus, the model provides accurate and reliable explanations and promote confidence among the patients as well as medical professionals.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of JT-CoMP-CNOMA Networks with Imperfect CSI and SIC: A SWIPT-Empowered Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: This paper considers the simultaneous transmission of a coordinated multipoint cooperative non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) network while taking into account the interference of poor channel state information and successive interference cancellation. It is considered to be accurate that BSs and cell edge users do not have physical contact. Using the energy obtained from simultaneous wireless information and power transfer, each base station, according to NOMA, provides information about the cell edge user and the cell center user to the cell center user, who uses it to decode the information sent by both users and forward it to the cell edge user. To evaluate the performance of the suggested system, the closed-form formula for each user is represented in terms of outage probability. According to the results, there is an erroneous floor in the outage probability as a result of imperfect channel state information (ipCSI) and imperfect successive interference cancellation (ipSIC). It has been noted that ipCSI and ipSIC both significantly impair system performance. Simulations with Monte Carlo methods are used to validate the analytical results.

Author Keywords: Joint transmission coordinated multipoint cooperative NOMA (JT-CoMP CNOMA)
simultaneous wireless infor-mation and power transfer (SWIPT)

articleTitle: Emotion Categorization on Multiclass Textual Data Using ML and Ensemble Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: Emotion recognition involves interpreting individuals' emotional states, utilizing cues like facial expressions, body language, voice tone, and physiological signals. This study uses Natural Language Processing and extensively explores models such as SVM, Naive Bayes, Decision Tree, Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, AdaBoost, Gradient Boosting, Bagging, and Ensemble Model. The objective is to identify the most effective model for nuanced emotion classification from textual data, focusing on the WASSA dataset for a multiclass classification problem covering four emotions: anger, fear, sadness, and joy. Meticulous analysis of these algorithms delves into the intricate fabric of written language, deciphering a spectrum of emotional states. The ensemble model (SVM + XGBoost) achieves an accuracy of 0.90 and an F-measure of 0.90. Methodical experimentation and evaluation contribute profound insights to optimize emotion recognition methodologies, significantly advancing the interpretation of emotions expressed in the text within the evolving landscape.

articleTitle: Harnessing Insights from Streams: Unlocking Real-Time Data Flow with Docker and Cassandra in the Apache Ecosystem
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: Real-time data streaming pipelines are immensely valuable in today's data-driven world since they enable continuous data processing and analytics. This research paper provides a comprehensive exploration of the architecture, development, and deployment of an advanced real-time data streaming pipeline. It utilizes Docker for containerization, Apache Kafka for distributed streaming, Apache Spark for dynamic data transformation, and Cassandra for efficient NoSQL storage. The study outlines the intricacies of integrating these technologies, examining the pipeline's components, functionalities, performance metrics, and potential applications. Through this case study, the paper show-cases the efficacy of open-source tools in constructing highly scalable and resilient data streaming pipelines.

articleTitle: Auto-correlation and Fisher Face Algorithm based gender recognition using Voice and facial images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: This work focuses on classifying speakers' gender based on their voice and facial features. These systems are useful for a number of things, including marketing, healthcare, user authentication, security, and more. We incorporated it to achieve high accuracy because gender recognition using voice or face, as implemented in the Uni-modal (facial images, voice samples) framework, suffers from poor accuracy. utilized a person's biological and behavioural traits as an input in this instance. The goal is to use the Auto-correlation method to estimate the speaker's gender from a speech sample, and Fisher face algorithm to identify the speaker's gender from a picture of their face, and integration of the results to improve the gender classifier's accuracy. A database containing voice and visual samples of both male and female pupils has been taken into consideration.

articleTitle: An Integrated Deep Learning Approach for Crack Detection and Localization in Tyre Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: The production of tyres plays a crucial role in the expansion of the automotive sector. The journey from the first pneumatic tyre to the development of high-performance tyres has been a gradual process for the auto industry. Despite the extensive integration of artificial intelligence in manufacturing and production, the identification of cracks and defects in tyres still heavily relies on human inspection. This manual process is time-consuming and prone to inaccuracies, adversely affecting overall output. This study addresses these challenges by employing ResNet50 for the classification of normal and cracked tyres, and the YOLO (You Only Look Once) object detection algorithm for crack detection and localization. The utilization of ResNet50 and YOLO in this study offers a transformative solution to the challenges plaguing the tyre production sector. By harnessing ResNet50 for the classification of normal and cracked tyres, and integrating YOLO for precise crack detection and localization, this research significantly enhances the efficiency and accuracy of tyre inspection processes. With ResNet50 achieving an impressive average accuracy of 92.65% in tyre image classification and YOLOv5 demonstrating a remarkable mean average precision (mAP) of 94.95%, this composition not only streamlines operations but also elevates quality control standards. This technological advancement promises to reduce manual labor, mitigate inaccuracies, and ultimately bolster the automotive industry's overall output and reliability.

articleTitle: Enhancing Quality Control of Steel Coils with Real-Time Edge Defect Detection Based on Computer Vision and Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: Steel has emerged as a vital component in various industries, ranging from small tools to large-scale structures like ships and statues. With the increasing demand for steel, the steel manufacturing sector has witnessed significant growth and a corresponding rise in production. However, ensuring high-quality steel has become a paramount concern for producers. Defective steel can have severe consequences during downstream manufacturing processes, leading to accidents and product failures. Consequently, steel industry giants have recognized the need for real-time edge defect detection in steel coils at the strip producing mill, as early detection allows for timely corrective actions. To address this challenge, this research leverages computer vision and deep learning techniques, specifically custom-built defect datasets collected from the industry itself, sourced from AM/NS India. Considering the diverse range of AI-ML methodologies available, the proposed method adopts convolutional neural network (CNN) and advanced CNN-based models such as SSD, Mask RCNN, and Faster RCNN, aiming to identify the most optimal model for building a Real-time Edge Defect Detection System. This research tackles the limitations associated with manual inspection of steel coils by automating the process. By implementing this approach, disruptions in coil transportation can be eliminated, the occurrence of expensive product failures can be minimized, and overall production efficiency can be enhanced. The proposed computer vision-based deep learning approach, once trained and deployed with accurate datasets and dependencies, will introduce a new level of accuracy and advancement in the steel industry's defect detection capabilities.

articleTitle: SafeSync: A Comprehensive Safety and Monitoring System for Two-Wheeler Users Using Machine Learning, ESP32, GPS, and GSM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: Our work, “SafeSync” proposes a complete safety and monitoring system aimed to address the considerable hazards encountered by two-wheeler users, such as accidents and rash driving scenarios. Unlike other systems, SafeSync combines powerful technology such as ESP32, GPS, and GSM with an innovative application of machine learning methods. This system specializes in detecting and alerting to accidents, tracking vehicles in real time, and identifying risky driving behaviour. SafeSync goes beyond traditional safety measures by not only identifying ongoing accidents but also forecasting potential events. This predictive feature enables the system to proactively inform users or authorities in advance, assisting in the prevention of accidents. The Flutter-built dedicated mobile app serves as a user-friendly interface, offering real-time updates on the vehicle's status and location. The program also allows users to customise monitoring settings and add parental restrictions. By actively recognizing and warning users to dangerous practises, SafeSync strives to improve rider safety and promote responsible driving behaviour. Finally, the initiative helps overall road safety by providing a solid solution for two-wheeler users to monitor and enhance their road safety.

articleTitle: Applications and Approaches of Sentiment Analysis: A Current Review
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: Limitless amount of data is loaded in every moment in social media platforms in the forms of audio, videos, texts, and photos. They are rich sources of information, which has immense value. Hence extraction of information from them is inevitable. Many methods are employed for this and the popular among them to mine the information is sentiment analysis. To materialize the objectives of this study, a systematic review of articles published from 2013 to 2023 was done. Our study reviewed the relevance of sentiment analysis in social media by probing the different approaches followed, the platforms used and its applications, as its main objectives. Its results show that majority of studies applied machine learning approach or hybrid method for executing sentiment analysis.

articleTitle: Enhanced MRI Reconstruction using Compressed Sensing and Sparse Representation Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel method for image reconstruction in the context of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). The goal of our work is to improve the reconstruction quality while reducing the number of measurements that is required, and thus enabling faster imaging thus reducing the burden on patients. An Edge Enhanced Sampling pattern is introduced in this paper,a custom pattern based on the image's edge map, which utilises the edge information and develops the sampling pattern. We compare the method proposed with three existing patterns like random, Cartesian grid and radial and demonstrate its better performance. These patterns determine which measurements are acquired during the MRI scan. We generate these patterns based on the desired acceleration factor, which represents the reduction in the number of measurements compared to the original Nyquist rate. Overall, our work demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed method in achieving high-quality image reconstruction from undersampled k-space data in MRI. This has the potential to significantly enhance the efficiency and speed of MRI scans, leading to improved patient experiences and better healthcare outcomes.

articleTitle: Leukaemia: A Comparative Analysis of Deep Learning Models Using ALL Dataset
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: White blood cells, also known as leukocytes, or WBCs, spread abnormally in the bone marrow and blood, resulting in leukaemia (blood cancer). Leukaemia can be identified by pathologists by examining a patient's blood sample under a microscope. By counting different blood cells and physical characteristics, they can identify and classify leukaemia. This method takes a lot of time to forecast leukaemia. The pathologist's professional qualifications and experiences may also have an impact on this process. Traditional machine learning and deep learning techniques in computer vision are useful road maps that improve the precision and speed of identifying and categorizing medical images, such as minuscule blood cells. This paper offers a thorough analysis of the different Deep CNN models for identification and classification of WBCs and acute leukaemia in microscopic blood cells.

articleTitle: Autonomous IoT-Integrated Tomato Plant Disease Detection: Harnessing YOLOv8 Algorithm and Micro-Navigation for Precision Agriculture
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: The nation of India, with abundant biodiversity, must contend with the effects of climate change on ecosystems and habitats. The tomato, or Solanum lycopersicum, is a critically important fruit utilized extensively in Indian and Western cuisines. However, the tomato is a fruit that may contract illness because of pest infestations, bacterial activity, microbes, and changes in the climate. Given the necessity for mass production, which renders “hand-picking” unfeasible, automation of a tomato field would be crucial. This would necessitate innovative solutions for disease diagnosis and classification in a large-scale production. This study examines various approaches related to tomato iden-tification, emphasizing performance analysis. To detect pests and illnesses in crops, the suggested method includes an autonomous mobile robot fitted with sensors, such as RGB cameras and Ultrasonic Sensors enhanced with Wi-Fi-enabled data transfer for IoT technology. The RGB camera takes crop visuals in real time and uses image processing, deep learning techniques, and the YOLOv8 algorithm to identify disease symptoms. To make the suggested mobile robot, an effective and long-lasting instrument for disease management in agriculture Micro-ROS is used. Its ability to identify illnesses quickly reduces the environmental impact and guarantees food safety, which is a big step toward a sustainable agricultural future.

articleTitle: A Machine Learning Approach for Credit Card Fraud Detection in Massive Datasets Using SMOTE and Random Sampling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: The surge in digital transactions has paved the way for an alarming rise in credit card fraud, compelling the need for robust detection systems. The swift progress of technology has transformed customer payment habits, driving them toward a cashless society, with the rise of digital payments making it easier for fraudsters to commit fraud. The impact of credit card fraud on revenue can be significant. No matter the scale of the businesses, credit card fraud will have a significant effect on the businesses. This paper addresses the escalating threat by proposing a fraud detection model utilizing the ’IEEE CIS Credit Fraud Detection’ dataset from Kaggle, constructing a machine learning model aimed at enhancing the accuracy of fraudulent transaction identification, presenting an integrated approach to credit card fraud detection that combines user separation and innovative techniques for improved accuracy and real-world impact, ultimately strengthening the global financial ecosystem.

articleTitle: Crop Damage Detection using Machine Learning Approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: Agriculture is of vital importance to human life as it is the main source of livestock production and contributes significantly to the country's employment opportunities and economy. Ensuring high standards of production quality is essential. Recent technological advances are merging agricultural and machine learning techniques to help improve crop quality. The main objective of this work is to make use of machine learning approaches to identify the healthy status of the crop. Multi-class classification is applied to the dataset which helps classify crop conditions. As there is an imbalance of data of the 3 classes, Random under- sampling and Tomek under-sampling methods are applied on the dataset. A combination of Tomek undersampling and Smote undersampling has also been performed on this dataset. Various algorithms like Gradient Boosting, Gaussian Naïve Bayes, Neural Network (MLP) and k-Nearest Neighbors were performed on the dataset which helped show that Randomforest was the best model in terms of accuracy and F1 score.

articleTitle: Machine Learning in Guided Reading Program Levelling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: This study addresses the challenge of optimizing a guided reading program through the integration of machine learning models, with a specific focus on levelling students up. Investigating the use of machine learning models for this purpose, the research identifies random forest as the most effective model for precision and personalization in assessments. The analysis of SHAP values emphasizes the crucial role of reading accuracy and comprehension in achieving this optimization. Despite limitations in duration and dataset size, the findings significantly contribute to understanding the potential of machine learning in educational settings. Future research endeavors seek to overcome these limitations, diversify datasets, and explore findings’ adaptability for ESL learners. The study concludes with a commitment to ongoing efforts in autonomously exploring the guided reading application's effectiveness, user-friendliness, and the role of machine learning in shaping personalized learning experiences.

articleTitle: Advancing Personality Detection through Word Embedments and Deep Learning: An Examination Using the MBTI Dataset
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: Personality detection and classification hold significant potential for enhancing decision-making processes and optimizing outcomes across various sectors. This interdisciplinary field finds applicative relevance in numerous domains such as business, healthcare, education, and personal development. In an effort to contribute to this burgeoning area of research, this paper introduces a comprehensive model specifically designed for personality detection. The model is rigorously tested on the Myers-Briggs Type Indicator (MBTI) dataset, a widely recognized framework in personality typology. The core of this proposed model lies in its innovative integration of four advanced word embeddings: Keras, Word2Vec, Glove, and FastText. These embeddings are coupled with cutting-edge deep learning architectures, including Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, Bidirectional LSTM (BI-LSTM), a hybrid of CNN and LSTM, and Gated Recurrent Units (GRU). This amalgamation results in a suite of 18 distinct models, each offering unique insights into personality classification. The implementation of these models is meticulously undertaken, and the outcomes are documented in detail. The results of this research which is 82% of accuracy, not only demonstrate the efficacy of combining various word embeddings with deep learning techniques but also pave the way for future explorations in the field of personality detection and classification.

articleTitle: Enhancing Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia Diagnosis Through Dual Deep Learning Approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: Leukemia, a life-threatening blood cancer, de-mands early and accurate diagnosis for effective treatment. This project aims to bring out the potential of dual deep learning techniques to enhance acute lymphoblastic leukemia detection. Our approach combines the capabilities of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). We also propose a mobile application that integrates these dual deep learning models to provide a user-friendly and accessible solution for acute lymphoblastic leukemia detection. High-resolution medical images, such as peripheral blood smears undergo thorough examination using advanced CNN architectures. Sequential data, encompassing temporal information like cell morphology evolution, genetic markers, and patient histories, are systematically analyzed. The dual deep learning model is trained on an extensive and diverse leukemia dataset, encompassing various subtypes and disease stages. Fine-tuning and transfer learning techniques are employed to optimize model performance. Once trained, the system is assured to efficiently evaluate new patient data,providing rapid and highly accurate leukemia diagnosis. The app is trained by using a comprehensive dataset of annotated blood cell images. The app will be designed with a user-friendly interface, enabling medical professionals to easily upload and analyze blood samples. The system's output will provide rapid and accurate leukemia detection, reducing the time and subjectivity associated with manual diagnosis. In summary our project aims to advance acute lymphoblastic leukemia detection by combining two or more powerful deep learning methods to work together effectively. This system holds the promise of assisting healthcare practitioners in making more informed decisions, ultimately leading to improved patient outcomes and more effective management of this life-threatening disease

articleTitle: Pulmonary Disease Multiclassification of Chest X-ray Images using Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: This research paper provides a novel approach for identifying lung illnesses using X-ray pictures, with an emphasis on distinguishing between five major respiratory ailments and a conventional lung classification. The proposed model evaluates X-ray images and produces exact classification results for pneumonia, COVID-19, and a typical lung using cutting-edge deep learning approaches such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), DenseNet, MobileNet, and Inception. Using a diverse and extensively annotated dataset, the model is subjected to rigorous training and validation techniques that maximize its ability to detect minute patterns that may be indicative of certain diseases. This will help to enhance automated diagnostic tools for prompt and effective medical interventions. This study investigates a novel use of X-ray imaging for the diagnosis of lung diseases, including Pneumonia, Covid 19 and a normal standard lung. Consider X-rays as unique superhero eyes that have the ability to peer into our chests. Computers have been trained by scientists to recognize lung diseases in patients based on X-ray images. Authors are assisting physicians in identifying and treating these lung issues more quickly by teaching computers to recognize these signs.

articleTitle: An Automated System for Question Generation and Answer Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: An innovative educational tool called the “Auto-mated Question Generation and Answer Evaluation System” was created to make the assessment process more efficient. By automating the creation of questions, it conforms to curriculum standards for a broad range of subjects and ability levels. More-over, it makes use of sophisticated machine learning and Natural Language Processing (NLP) methods to thoroughly assess student responses and offer tailored feedback that surpasses traditional grading. This system promises to be a useful tool in contemporary education because it increases educational efficiency, encour-ages personalised learning, maintains fairness, and continuously adapts through machine learning. This signifies a noteworthy progression in the mechanisation of question formulation and response evaluation. Through the utilisation of natural language processing and machine learning, this system provides educators, content creators, and learners with an adaptable tool that enhances learning, content creation, and assessment procedures in a variety of fields.

articleTitle: PI Controller Based Modified ZETA Converter with Higher Voltage Gain for Load Voltage Regulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: This project aims to design, implement, and analyze a PI controller-based modification of the ZETA converter with the objective of achieving higher voltage gain for improved load voltage regulation. The ZETA converter is chosen for its simplicity, reliability, and inherent advantages, and the integration of a PI controller is proposed to enhance its performance in regulating load voltage. The modification involves carefully adjusting the converter's parameters to achieve a higher voltage gain while maintaining the desirable features of the ZETA converter, such as reduced input ripple current. The PI controller is employed to dynamically adjust the converter's operation in response to varying load conditions, ensuring optimal performance across a range of operational scenarios. The project involves a comprehensive study of the modified ZETA converter's behavior under different load conditions through simulation and practical implementation. The PI controller's proportional, integral, and derivative actions are fine-tuned to achieve improved transient response, reduced steady-state errors, and enhanced stability in load voltage regulation. Comparative analysis with traditional ZETA converters will be conducted to highlight the advantages of the proposed modification. Simulation results and experimental validations demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed converter with supply battery achieving superior load voltage regulation compared to traditional ZETA converters.

articleTitle: Computationally Efficient Machine Learning Methodology for Indian Nobel Laureate Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems (RAICS)
abstract: A computationally efficient methodology for Indian Nobel Laureate classification is proposed in this study, emphasizing the optimization of image categorization through supervised learning techniques. Leveraging advancements in Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), the research aims to enhance the efficiency and precision of image classification tasks.
